rule: Product extension register. Every DI service override (INopStartup Order >= 3000), repository decorator, global action or result filter, middleware, Nop.Web model-factory override, ModelReceivedEvent veto and registered core modification installed by a product plugin is listed in BR-ADM-002 to BR-ADM-008 with target, mechanism, owning feature, provider features and the rule that specifies it. One owner per overridden interface (decision OVR-REG): other features plug in through the provider interface the owner publishes and never register their own implementation. One owner per intercepted decision on a native action (decision SINGLE-FILTER): the impersonation action (IAM-026, rule providers IC-IAM-09), the two native download actions (SEC-002, rule providers IC-SEC-05) and every upload action (ADM-008, upload contexts IC-ADM-08) carry exactly one product filter for that decision; other features supply rules to it and register no filter of their own for it. Several global action filters may run on one action when each checks a different thing; each is listed with its filter order (Proposed) and refuses independently. Filters identify an action by controller and method name, because some route names differ from the method (Impersonate and ApplyVendorSubmit are routed as Edit and ApplyVendor). The ADM start-up check reads the IServiceCollection and reports, as a system warning, an interface with more than one product implementation or with an implementation from a plugin other than its owner. A chapter that adds or removes an entry updates this register in the same change.

A workflow definition is published only if every path reaches an end, every exclusive gateway has a default path, every parallel join matches its split and every step type is available for the client.

Workflow steps and approval decisions never change native or module state directly: they call the owning module's service (which uses the native service, for example IOrderProcessingService). Event consumers only enqueue start or signal requests, carrying an idempotency key; the engine runner (scheduled task) processes them, because nopCommerce event consumers swallow exceptions.
Simulation and rule testing have no side effects: no notification, document, external call, payment or production log entry.
The rule language is declarative and constrained: operators over declared facts only; no code, reflection, file, network or database access.

A rule cannot be activated while it conflicts (same rule set, overlapping matches in the test data, different outcomes) unless a precedence order resolves it; strategies are first match by priority or all matches.

An approval item is visible and actionable only to users whose role is named on the current step, within their authority limit or by active delegation; the requester never approves own items and one user decides at most one step of an item.

An owning module may implement a pre-decision guard for its object types (IC-ADM-03 CanDecide). ADM calls it before recording an approval, an approval with conditions or the confirmation of conditions; a refusal records nothing and shows Adm.DecisionBlocked with the module reason. The OnApproved callback still re-checks, and a callback error leaves the item decided and raises an ADM-009 exception, as before.
A transaction parameter marked Fixed cannot be changed on a transaction; a Required parameter must be present; overrides need a reason and are recorded as deviations (PLT BR-PLT-017).

Eligibility affects visibility only through native ACL by customer role: eligibility rules compute role membership; purchase limits and quotas are enforced by an ADM cart rule provider (IC-CHK-01) of the CHK-003 IShoppingCartService override, which PlaceOrderAsync re-runs, and reserved at placement by an ADM placement participant (IC-CHK-06, Reserve / Confirm / Release, BR-CHK-020) of the CHK-003 override. ADM overrides neither IShoppingCartService nor IOrderProcessingService (OVR-REG).

rule: Upload policy: ADM-008 is the single owner of server-side upload checks (file type, size, file signature, virus scan) for every upload in the product. Each upload belongs to one context: an ADM context of the native action, or a context that a module registers through IC-ADM-08 (with a resolver for native actions, or a CheckUpload call from its own endpoint); a resolver match takes precedence over the ADM default context. A file that reaches the IFormFile backstop from an endpoint with no context gets the ADM context other upload (Proposed; values not stated). Files a module receives as bytes (APIs, mailboxes, apps) are covered only through CheckUpload, because the backstop sees IFormFile uploads only. The stricter of the native per-field limit and the context policy applies. The policy is enforced before the file is stored, by one ADM global action filter on the upload actions listed in BR-ADM-006 and BR-ADM-007 and by the IDownloadService / IPictureService overrides as backstop; scanning happens before storage. No other module keeps a file-type or size check or registers an upload filter; SEC-002 records upload ownership on the same actions and checks nothing about the file.
basis: REQ-MPC-FR-324; FIT (DownloadService, PictureService public virtual); SINGLE-FILTER

rule: Every exception resolution records operator, action, reason code, comment and outcome; bulk actions are allowed only for actions the exception type declares batch-safe.

Work-queue items (approval items, exceptions and items raised into the console by other modules) record assignment, completion and reopen events with assignee, actor and time; RPT-009 reads them for operator metrics.

ADM messages are sent only through TRK-005. ADM registers its event codes through IC-TRK-04 RegisterEventCode at installation (names Proposed): Administration.ApprovalAssigned, Administration.ApprovalDecided (approved, approved with conditions, rejected with reason and recourse), Administration.WorkflowCaseFailed, Administration.AlertRaised, Administration.UploadInfected (administrator summary) and Administration.ScreeningMatch. A workflow notification step (ADM-002) may name only an event code registered with TRK-005; alert rules (ADM-010) send through TRK-005 on the channels of the rule.

ADM settings are listed in the ADM key catalogue (key, type, layer, secret flag, default); antivirus-engine and sanctions-provider credentials are flagged secret, so packs refuse them and exports omit them (BR-PLT-013). ADM pages, widgets, filters, providers and scheduled tasks check the feature state for the store through IC-PLT-02 before acting. ADM registers the rule evaluation log and work drafts as PLT-020 record types (IC-PLT-08). ADM writes only through IRepository<> and writes business audit events through IC-SEC-01.

The chatbot answers only from approved scripted responses (current approved version, CRM-007) and published content; it never states order, payment or account data that it did not read from native services, and it says it has no answer rather than guess.

AI output is a suggestion: generated text, translations (when approval is on), images, prices, drafts, OCR fields, ID checks, inspections and scores change no record and decide nothing about a person until a person accepts or decides.
Order data in a chat is given only to the signed-in customer, or on WhatsApp to the phone number of the order's customer; "not found" and "not yours" get the same reply.

Native AI generation actions are allowed only to users holding the native create-edit-delete permission of the entity concerned; the AI plugin adds an action filter for Admin ArtificialIntelligenceController.GenerateMetaTags, which has no CheckPermission attribute; the filter is listed in the ADM extension register (BR-ADM-001).

Content sent to an external AI or translation provider is limited to the fields needed; personal data is sent only where the AI use register entry allows it and the country profile (SEC-012) permits it; recommendation events carry only a pseudonymous customer key.

Every AI setting key is listed in the AI plugin key catalogue (key, type, layer, secret flag, default) so pack validation accepts it; every key, token or credential setting (native AI and translation keys as listed in BR-PLT-013, and the keys of the OCR, ID-check, ML and image services) is flagged secret, so packs refuse it and exports omit it. AI widgets, routing and scheduled work act for a store only when IC-PLT-02 IsEnabled returns true for the AI feature concerned.
Every chatbot conversation starts with the AI disclosure; every AI-generated item shown to a customer carries the AI label.
Every model that scores or ranks people stores its version and main reasons per result and has a bias-report link per monitoring period in the AI use register.

A category is shown to a shopper only if it is published, allowed by ACL for one of the shopper's roles and mapped to the current store (native; catalogsettings.ignoreacl and ignorestorelimitations must be false where segmentation is used).

A listing can be submitted for review or published only when it has: name; full description; price (unless CallForPrice); stock quantity when stock is managed; at least one picture; every field and attribute required by the category schemas of all its categories (CAT-005); the cross-border fields when offered for international delivery (CAT-015); the regulatory fields and a valid certificate when its category is regulated (CAT-019). The check runs at the transition, not at the first save, because pictures are added after the product exists in the native editor.

CAT adds no upload filter or type check of its own (one owner per behaviour, decision on upload types). The upload actions of CAT's own admin pages (360 image sets and brochures CAT-016, certificates CAT-019, provenance documents CAT-020, takedown evidence CAT-021, import files CAT-009) are registered with ADM-008 under the contexts admin picture, admin download and data imports, so the ADM-008 filter covers them; CAT forwards the file to IPictureService / IDownloadService, where the ADM-008 backstop also applies. Product documents cannot be told apart from other admin downloads, because DownloadController.AsyncUpload takes no product argument; product pictures can, because ProductPictureAdd takes the product ID and inserts each file through IPictureService.InsertPictureAsync. Native behaviour kept: fixed image extension list and SVG switch (mediasettings.allowsvguploads); images larger than mediasettings.maximumimagesize pixels are resized, not refused.
basis: REQ-MPC-FR-060; see ADM-008 (BR-ADM-060); FIT (PictureService.InsertPictureAsync(IFormFile): imgExt list; Admin ProductController.ProductPictureAdd(int productId, IFormCollection form) inserts each file through InsertPictureAsync, endpoint set in Views/Product/_CreateOrUpdate.Multimedia.Pictures.cshtml; DownloadController.cs:93 AsyncUpload: no product argument, no type or size check)

rule: SKUs are unique across products and attribute combinations. When a product is inserted with an empty SKU, the CAT IProductService.InsertProductAsync / InsertProductsAsync override generates it from the active pattern; the sequence is read and advanced under ILocker key 'cat-sku-{PatternId}'; if PerformActionWithLockAsync returns false after the configured retries the insert is refused (Cat.SkuGenerationBusy). Sequence numbers are never reused.

Product.Published is true only while the listing state (SM-CAT-01) is Published. Enforced by: (a) a ModelReceivedEvent<BaseNopModel> consumer that adds a ModelState error (Cat.PublishNotAllowed) on Admin ProductController.Create and Edit [POST], which both check ModelState.IsValid; (b) the IProductService DI override hosted by CAT-002 (INopStartup Order >= 3000), through the publish-gate provider that CAT-022 registers (IC-CAT-04), whose InsertProductAsync, InsertProductsAsync, UpdateProductAsync and UpdateProductsAsync force Published = false for any product not in state Published — this covers BulkEditSave, CopyProduct / CopyProductService, ImportManager, the API and the native low-stock re-publish in ApplyLowStockActivityAsync (catalogsettings.publishbackproductwhencancellingorders); (c) catalogsettings.allowviewunpublishedproductpage = false. Only the CAT lifecycle service sets Published = true, and only after the publish guard passes (IC-CAT-04: no vendor pause reason, BR-CAT-030; SEL CheckEligibility, IC-SEL-01). An update that would set Published from false to true for a listing in state Published (native low-stock re-publish) runs the same guard; on Fail Published is saved false and the listing moves to Paused with reason NotEligible. Native ProductService.SearchProductsAsync does not filter by vendor status, so storefront hiding of a suspended seller relies on this gate.
basis: D (CAT-022); FIT (ProductController.cs:1083-1093, 1227-1252, 983-996, 1524-1539; ProductService.cs:165-185, 590-623; ImportManager.cs:2607-2619; Web ProductController.cs:137; no Product repository insert or update outside ProductService in Libraries, Plugins or Presentation)

rule: An approval step is decided only by a holder of Misc.Catalogue.Listings.Approve assigned to that step; the user who submitted the listing cannot decide any step of it; reject and request-changes need a reason.

On submission the listing goes to the queue of the first active assignment rule that matches (dimensions: category, seller, seller tier, store), in priority order; with no match it goes to the default queue. Changing rules does not move listings already in review.

An edit by the seller of a listing in InReview withdraws the submission (back to Draft). An edit by the seller of a Published listing that changes a field in the re-approval set moves it to InReview with Published false until approved; the re-approval field set is a setting (default not stated). Edits by users holding Misc.Catalogue.Listings.Approve do not change the state.

A category schema change is a draft version until a different user with Misc.Catalogue.Schema.Approve approves it; it then applies to submissions made after approval; published listings that miss a new required field stay published and are listed for their owners.
Missing required fields block submission; image-quality findings (minimum pixel size, setting) only warn.

Prohibited rules (category, item, term) with action Block or Flag are applied to name, short and full description in every language and to category mappings, at submission, import validation (CAT-010), API create/update (CAT-011) and Q&A text (CAT-018). Block refuses; Flag routes to review with the reason.
A bulk file is imported only after a validation run with zero errors (all or nothing); the validation report is kept with the import job.
A listing report or takedown that is upheld withdraws the listing with the decision reason; evidence files are kept; every decision is audited.

Every product save writes a version snapshot (product fields, localized values, category and specification attribute mappings, tier prices, picture references). Restoring creates a new version and is subject to BR-CAT-005 and BR-CAT-008. Autosave writes only to a per-user draft buffer, never to the product.

Withdrawal needs a reason, sets state Withdrawn and Published false, notifies watchers once and raises Listing.Withdrawn. Consumers of Listing.Withdrawn in other modules only enqueue work; CAT changes no order, payment or case.

A bundle is a product whose components are required attribute mappings with one preselected AssociatedToProduct value each (AssociatedProductId, Quantity, PriceAdjustment 0); the bundle price is the bundle product's price; component stock and availability are handled natively; a seller bundles only own products.

A call-for-price product cannot be added to the cart directly (native). The CAT product-page button creates a Misc.RFQ request for that product; a cart item created from an accepted Misc.RFQ quote (QuoteItem.ShoppingCartItemId set) is exempt from the native Products.CallForPrice warning. The exemption is a CAT provider of the CHK-003 IShoppingCartService host (decision OVR-REG, BR-CAT-032); CAT does not override ShoppingCartService.
basis: D; OVR-REG; FIT (ShoppingCartService.GetStandardWarningsAsync:380-385; RfqService.CreateShoppingCartAsync inserts through the repository; GetQuoteItemByShoppingCartItemIdAsync)

rule: Compliance status follows SM-CAT-03; a Barred listing cannot be submitted or published; an expired certificate pauses the listing when auto-hide is on for its category.
A product edit form carries the version number it was opened with (hidden field added by a CAT admin widget); the Edit [POST] veto refuses the save when a newer version exists (Cat.EditConflict).

Price precedence for a customer, product and quantity (nopCommerce 5.00): accepted quote item (Misc.RFQ, GetShoppingCartItemUnitPriceEvent) > native tier price, when one applies > native price-list price of the customer or one of the customer's roles (CAT-039; CatalogSettings.PriceListStrategy between lists) > product price; native discounts apply to the result. A fixed currency price (CAT-042) replaces the converted price only when no price list of the customer contains the product within its dates (checked through IPriceListService with the same filter as the native method), so a contract price is never replaced by a list price in another currency. Price lists are applied by the native base method inside its cached block; the CAT-042 host never applies them again. Fixed currency prices are applied outside the native cached block of PriceCalculationService.GetFinalPriceAsync, whose cache key holds product, quantity, customer role IDs and store but not the customer or currency.
basis: FIT (PriceCalculationService.cs:77-140, 414-470; NopCatalogDefaults.ProductPriceCacheKey; ShoppingCartService.GetUnitPriceAsync, ShoppingCartService.cs:1401-1405); PRICE-500; Proposed (fixed currency price versus price list)

rule: Bookings and slot capacity change only through the CAT booking service (IC-CAT-07): Hold (cart), Confirm (order placed), Book (direct, for EGV-003, no cart), Move, RecordOutcome, Release and slot writes from SVC GenerateSlots. A place is taken under ILocker key 'cat-slot-{SlotId}' only while held plus confirmed bookings are below capacity; a move takes both slot locks in ascending SlotId order; holds expire after the hold duration; confirmation links the hold to the order item; outcomes CancelledByCustomer and CancelledByProvider release the place, Attended, NoShowCustomer and NoShowProvider complete the booking; release on order cancellation is enqueued by a consumer and done by a task; a nightly task recounts capacity; generated capacity is never set below confirmed bookings.
basis: D; Proposed; (SM-SVC-02, BR-SVC-011); FIT (ShoppingCartItemMovedToOrderItemEvent, OrderStatusChangedEvent, ILocker)

rule: A promoted placement is active only between its approved start and end dates and while its product is Published; approvals never exceed the slot limit of the placement type on any day; the native flags (ShowOnHomepage, ProductCategory.IsFeaturedProduct) are set and cleared only by the placement task.

A cart line must meet OrderMinimumQuantity, OrderMaximumQuantity, AllowedQuantities (native) and the multiple-of rule (CAT); a quantity above the maximum is accepted only through an approved over-maximum request (IC-ADM-03 OnApproved) when that option is on for the product. The CAT checks run as providers of the CHK-003 IShoppingCartService host (BR-CAT-032).
Until UOM-01 is decided, quantities stay integers: a unit of measure has a base unit and a positive conversion factor; pack prices are base-unit count times price per base unit.

For an order in currency C with fixed prices, each line is stored in the primary store currency as fixed price divided by Order.CurrencyRate; the amount shown and charged to the customer in C equals the fixed price, rounded to the minor unit of C.

A Published listing is Stale when Product.UpdatedOnUtc is older than the stale period of its category (setting); the seller is reminded once; re-confirmation or an edit clears the flag; after the grace period it is paused with reason Stale if auto-pause is on.

A CAT feature that belongs to a pack (Marketplace, Services and bookings, B2B trade, Commerce extensions, Engagement and loyalty, Analytics) checks its feature state through IC-PLT-02 IsEnabled (setting productfeature.<prd-id>, store value else shared value) before it shows a page or widget, accepts a provider call or runs scheduled work for a store; a feature that is off for the store does nothing for that store. Always-on features (including the hosts CAT-022 and CAT-042) do not check.

Every new CAT setting key is listed in the CAT plugin key catalogue with key, type, layer, secret flag and default so that pack validation accepts it (NFR-X-008). Keys that hold a credential, key or token are flagged secret, so the pack loader refuses them and exports omit them (CFG-01): feed target credentials (CAT-035) and the map provider key (CAT-028). Native translation and AI keys (translationsettings, artificialintelligencesettings) are native settings entered per client instance.

CAT business audit events AUD-CAT-nnn are written through IC-SEC-01 IAuditTrail.WriteAsync with a correlation id; old and new values of entity changes come from the SEC IRepository<> decorator and need no call. CAT plugin tables are written only through IRepository<>; CAT never writes through INopDataProvider directly. The native activity log is not used as audit.

Vendor listing pause: SEL pauses and resumes all listings of a vendor through IC-CAT-03 PauseListings / ResumeListings with one of the reason codes Vacation, SellerSuspended, SellerBlacklisted, DocumentExpired, CommissionOverdue, PerformanceIntervention, under ILocker key 'cat-vendor-listings-{VendorId}'. While a vendor has any pause reason, its Published listings are Paused (listing reason VendorPause) and no listing of that vendor can be published by any path. A listing resumes only when neither its vendor nor the listing itself has a pause reason left and the publish guard passes. SEL never writes ListingState or Product.Published.

Decision OVR-REG: CAT is the only product plugin that overrides IProductService (host CAT-002, core; CAT-022 is its publish-gate provider), IPriceCalculationService and IOrderTotalCalculationService (CAT-042), each by one DI registration (INopStartup Order >= 3000) listed in the ADM extension register (BR-ADM-001). Other modules register providers (IC-CAT-04, IC-CAT-05, IC-CAT-06) and never register their own implementation of these interfaces. Each host first runs the native base method and then its providers in their declared order; a provider exception fails the call (it is not swallowed). A provider of a pack feature that is off for the store is skipped (BR-CAT-027).
basis: OVR-REG; FIT (L1 section 6.2 principle 7; ProductService, PriceCalculationService and OrderTotalCalculationService methods are public virtual)

rule: CAT does not override IShoppingCartService (owner CHK-003, decision OVR-REG). CAT cart checks are providers of the CHK-003 host through IC-CHK-01: multiple-of quantity (CAT-037), call-for-price exemption for Misc.RFQ quote items (BR-CAT-017), over-maximum exemption for approved requests (BR-CAT-023), service area (CAT-026), booking hold expiry (CAT-027). The two exemptions are registered replacers of the named native warnings Products.CallForPrice (quote lines) and ShoppingCart.MaximumQuantity (approved over-maximum lines); the host matches them by resource key, never by text (BR-CHK-015). All other CAT checks only add warnings.

Order-total adjustments (IC-CAT-06). Adjust is side-effect free and is called after the native GetShoppingCartTotalAsync result; a Deduction is between zero and the running total, a Charge is zero or more, the total is never below zero; the applied adjustments of the last calculation are kept for the current request. At placement CAT-042 is one IC-CHK-06 participant of the CHK-003 host: Reserve passes each provider exactly the amount used in the order total; Confirm, per saved sub-order and before OrderPlacedEvent, writes OrderTotalAdjustment rows and calls the provider Confirm, in which the provider writes its own money record (PAY-009 wallet ledger); Release reverses reservations when placement fails. On admin order edits the CAT override of the protected UpdateTotalAsync re-applies the stored amounts after the native total (a Deduction capped at the new total) and calls no provider. Adjustments are read through GetOrderAdjustments and the DOC token. CAT changes no wallet, premium or payment record itself.
basis: OVR-REG; WAL-01; Proposed; FIT (OrderTotalCalculationService.GetShoppingCartTotalAsync public virtual, UpdateTotalAsync protected virtual; OrderProcessingService.PreparePlaceOrderDetailsAsync calls GetShoppingCartTotalAsync once, OrderProcessingService.cs:399)

rule: Price-list configuration rules (decision PRICE-500): (1) a product in a contract price list carries no tier price for the same buyers, because natively the tier price replaces the price-list price; CAT lists every product where both apply (pricing-conflicts list) and sales staff remove the tier price or record acceptance; (2) catalogsettings.cacheproductprices stays off while any price list is assigned to individual customers, because the cached price is keyed by roles and store, not by customer; the B2B pack validation refuses the combination; (3) CatalogSettings.PriceListStrategy (MinimalPrice or UseByPriority) is a client setting; (4) price lists have no store or currency scope.
basis: PRICE-500; FIT (PriceCalculationService.cs:77-140, 426-462; NopCatalogDefaults.ProductPriceCacheKey; Libraries/Nop.Core/Domain/PriceLists/PriceList.cs); Proposed (conflicts list, pack validation)

rule: Save for later uses a native CustomWishlist per customer; moving a line between cart and list goes through IShoppingCartService so stock, price and quantity checks run.
Guest checkout is a per-client setting (OrderSettings.AnonymousCheckoutAllowed): KTDA on (CUS-006), Malawi Post off (FR-125). No code differs between clients.
Prices and totals are always calculated on the server at placement; no price or total sent by the browser is used.
The confirm page total is stored server-side when the page is shown; if the total calculated at placement differs, the order is not placed and the new total is shown (Chk.PriceChanged).

Placement validation runs inside the IOrderProcessingService.PlaceOrderAsync override, before payment, in this order: native cart and item warnings; price check (BR-CHK-004); eligibility (ACL, PAY-018 restriction, CHK-011 rules, CHK-018 approval, LOG-004 serviceability and seller coverage); payment method active and allowed by PAY routing rules (BR-PAY-001); PAY-018 risk evaluation. The first failure stops placement. Validation is not placed in event consumers (L1 §6.2 principle 8).

Placement host (core): the IOrderProcessingService override is one class for the product, owned by the core checkout feature CHK-003 (decision OVR-REG; L1 §6.2 principle 7; core behaviour is not hosted in an optional pack, D-01), registered in INopStartup with Order >= 3000. Its PlaceOrderAsync reproduces the native sequence once per checkout: when PlaceOrderWithLock is on, take the named Mutex keyed by customer once, check and later set NopOrderDefaults.OrderWithLockCacheKey once; prepare details once (PreparePlaceOrderDetailsAsync); run the IC-CHK-02 validators and the IC-CHK-06 Reserve phase; process payment once for the checkout; save the order (SaveOrderDetailsAsync) and move its cart lines; clear the cart once; publish OrderPlacedEvent and run CheckOrderStatusAsync per saved order. Without a registered order splitter one order is placed. When the Marketplace pack registers the CHK-004 order splitter (IC-CHK-11), the host saves one sub-order per group the splitter returns (SaveOrderDetailsAsync with a new OrderGuid per sub-order, moving only that group's cart lines); it never calls base.PlaceOrderAsync per sub-order, because base loads and clears the whole cart and would trip its own interval cache. Other modules plug in only through IC-CHK-02 validators, IC-CHK-06 placement participants, IC-CHK-07 order-action guards, IC-CHK-08 cancellation participants and the IC-CHK-11 splitter; the override is listed in the ADM extension register (BR-ADM-001). The host follows the 5.00.1 sequence: after the last order it calls IShoppingCartService.ResetCheckoutDataAsync (moved from ICustomerService) and SetShoppingCartVendorAsync(customer, null) once, and it sets the desired delivery date read once from the customer on every sub-order, because SaveOrderDetailsAsync copies it to the first order saved and clears it (OrderProcessingService.cs:790-797, 1634-1639). The override is rebased on the 5.00.1 OrderProcessingService (constructor and PlaceOrderAsync changed in 5.00).
basis: REQ-MPC-FR-110; FIT (OrderProcessingService 288-315, 723-817, 1283-1347, 1594-1720 in 5.00.1); L1 §6.3; OVR-REG; D-01; Proposed (host in CHK-003)

rule: Order-level amounts (delivery fee, payment fee, order discount, checkout-attribute fee, redeemed reward points, gift cards) are allocated to sub-orders in proportion to sub-order subtotals, except a delivery fee calculated per seller by LOG-002, which stays with that seller's sub-order; amounts are rounded to the currency's minor unit and the remainder goes to the sub-order with the largest subtotal.
Each sub-order has one seller; direct payment to a seller (PAY-035) is offered only when the checkout has one seller.
Lines are grouped into sub-orders by seller and fulfilment choice (delivery, or pickup at outlet X); each sub-order has one native PickupInStore value.

Delivery-window capacity is checked and reserved at placement under ILocker key 'chk-slot-{SlotId}-{Date}' by the CHK-006 placement participant (IC-CHK-06); a cancelled order releases its place through the CHK-006 cancellation participant (IC-CHK-08).
An address must have at least the locators the client rule requires (street address, landmark or pin); the rule is a client setting.
One CheckoutSession per customer and store is open at a time; its reference is unique, not guessable, and kept on every order it produced.

Acknowledgements and the terms checkbox are enforced on the server by a CHK global action filter on CheckoutController.ConfirmOrder and OpcConfirmOrder [POST]; a ModelReceivedEvent veto is not used because these actions take no model.

The notice set is taken from the e-transactions part of the store country's CountryPrivacyProfile (entity owned by SEC-012, fields owned by CHK-009, read through IC-SEC-03). Notice texts are native Topics; policy versions are MKT-008's (IC-MKT-03). Acknowledgements and the checkout terms acceptance are recorded by IAM through IC-IAM-05 RecordAcceptance; CHK stores only the link from the order to the IAM acceptance id (decision ONE-RECORD).

Under decision OVR-REG CHK-003 owns the only IShoppingCartService override (DI, INopStartup Order >= 3000, listed in the ADM extension register BR-ADM-001). It overrides GetShoppingCartItemWarningsAsync, GetShoppingCartWarningsAsync, the protected GetStandardWarningsAsync and GetRentalProductWarningsAsync to call cart check providers (IC-CHK-01) after the native checks, and GetSubTotalAsync to call the one line subtotal adjuster (IC-CHK-05, MKT-002). Providers run in their registered order and may only add warnings, except a provider registered as the replacer of a named native warning (CAT: Products.CallForPrice for quote lines; INV-004: stock warning with holds). A provider error refuses the item (Chk.CartCheckUnavailable). CHK-011 cart rules are one provider; no other module overrides the interface. The override subclasses the 5.00.1 ShoppingCartService, whose constructor and vendor / stash logic changed in 5.00; it calls the native warnings, including ShoppingCart.SelectVendorToCheckout, which never fires while VendorEnabled is off (BR-CHK-023); GetShoppingCartAsync now takes a list of cart types and ResetCheckoutDataAsync is an IShoppingCartService member.
basis: REQ-MPC-FR-111; FIT (ShoppingCartService 337, 1071, 1141, 1187, 1335 in 5.00.1); L1 §6.2 principle 7; OVR-REG

rule: A pickup code is single-use, bound to one sub-order and one outlet, stored only as a hash and locked after the configured number of failed attempts (CHK-012 setting). CHK-012 issues the code, checks it and counts attempts (IC-CHK-09); the LOG-012 handover step calls the check, stores the proof of collection, calls DeliverAsync and then marks the code used.

An assisted order is placed in an acting session started through Place order for customer and allowed by the single impersonation filter owned by IAM-026 (BR-IAM-130, decision SINGLE-FILTER; CHK adds no filter); CHK-013 records agent and outlet once per order in AssistedOrder (the only order-to-agent record; IAM keeps the session, the native order note names the agent) and serves it to other modules through IC-CHK-10. Agents act only for non-staff customers of their own outlet (IAM-008 scope).

Available credit = credit limit minus open receivables (PAY-033, read through IC-PAY-08 GetOpenReceivables) minus unpaid on-account orders; it is checked in the On account payment method under ILocker key 'chk-credit-{CreditAccountId}'.
An approval is valid only for the cart snapshot it was given for (hash of lines, quantities and total); the requester cannot approve own requests.

Placement participants (IC-CHK-06) work in two phases inside the CHK-003 override: Reserve after the validators and before payment, each under its own ILocker key (for example 'adm-quota-{quotaId}', 'mkt-discount-{DiscountId}', 'chk-slot-{SlotId}-{Date}', 'chk-credit-{CreditAccountId}', 'fin-scheme-{SchemeId}', and 'pay-wallet-{WalletId}' taken by PAY-009 inside the CAT-042 participant); Confirm per saved sub-order before OrderPlacedEvent; Release when a later reservation, the payment or the placement fails. A reservation not confirmed or released ends at its expiry (setting, default not stated). This closes the race between a cart check and the order insert for limits shared by different customers, which the native per-customer placement lock does not cover.
basis: FIT (OrderProcessingService named mutex per customer; ILocker); Proposed;,

rule: The CHK-003 override also wraps ShipAsync, ReadyForPickupAsync and DeliverAsync: it calls every order-action guard (IC-CHK-07) first and refuses with the guard message by raising an error, so every caller (admin, seller endpoints, TRK-002, LOG-012, API) is covered. It wraps CancelOrderAsync: the native method runs first, then cancellation participants (IC-CHK-08); a participant error is listed as a checkout exception and does not undo the cancellation. Shipment creation (IShipmentService.InsertShipmentAsync) is not part of this override: it belongs to the ORD-010 shipment-guard host (BR-ORD-050).
basis: OVR-REG; FIT (IOrderProcessingService; Admin OrderController.SetAsShipped error notification)

rule: Configuration rule (decision CART-500): ShoppingCartSettings.VendorEnabled and VendorRequired stay off in every store of every client. The product keeps one cart for all sellers and splits order and payment in CHK-004; the native per-seller cart of 5.00 (vendor selector, Stash cart type, warning ShoppingCart.SelectVendorToCheckout) is not used.

Paying once for several sub-orders needs PAY group payment (IC-CHK-04 = IC-PAY-02; adapters declare group support). A multi-seller checkout offers only methods that declare group support; if none does, or until PAY group payment is built, a cart with items of more than one seller cannot be confirmed when the Marketplace pack is on (cart warning Chk.MultiSellerNotSupported).
The mobile app uses only the public API under an INT-001 API client; it never reads the database directly.
The service worker caches only public catalogue pages, topics and static files; account, cart, checkout and order pages are never cached; actions that change data are never queued offline.

Every CHN setting key is listed in the CHN plugin key catalogue (key, type, layer, secret flag, default) so pack validation accepts it; every setting that holds a credential, key or token (SMS provider keys, push keys, facebookexternalauthsettings.clientsecret of the bundled ExternalAuth.Facebook plugin) is flagged secret, so packs refuse it and exports omit it; channel account credentials live in encrypted plugin-table fields (ChannelAccount.CredentialsRef). CHN pages, widgets, consumers and scheduled tasks act for a store only when IC-PLT-02 IsEnabled returns true for the CHN feature concerned.

TRK-005 decides which notification is sent, to whom and on which channel; CHN adapters implement IC-TRK-02 (Send with idempotency key = message id; DeliveryReceipt; capability flags) and only deliver and report status. The bundled Misc.Brevo plugin is not installed in a client instance, because IWorkflowMessageService belongs to TRK-005 (OVR-REG, BR-TRK-021); CHN registers no IWorkflowMessageService override. Only two kinds of CHN send are outside TRK-005 (decision MSG-ROUTE, BR-TRK-026): conversational replies in a conversation the customer started (IC-CHN-04 SendReply for CRM agents and AI-003; CHN-005 replies to inbound SMS commands) and one-time codes that reach CHN-005 from IAM-002 through IC-IAM-01; both respect TRK-006 opt-outs (BR-CHN-020).
basis: FIT (Misc.Brevo replaces IWorkflowMessageService); OVR-REG; MSG-ROUTE; L1 §6.2 principle 7

rule: Order data is given on USSD, IVR, SMS and bot channels only to the phone number or linked account of the order's customer; "not found" and "not yours" get the same answer.
Inbound callbacks from channel providers are verified (signature, token or source address as the provider supports) before they are processed; failures are logged and audited.
Channel account credentials are stored encrypted per client instance and never exported in configuration packs.

Inbound messages (WhatsApp, WeChat, Telegram) are first stored as ChannelMessage, then published as module event Channel.MessageReceived (consumers only notify or enqueue), then routed by the inbound handler: chatbot first when AI-003 is enabled for the channel, otherwise live chat (CRM-008) or CRM intake through IC-CRM-04, per the routing setting. Replies by people or the chatbot in a conversation the customer started go back through IC-CHN-04 SendReply, which calls IC-TRK-06 CheckAllowed before each send and sends nothing when Blocked; notifications go only through TRK-005.

TRK-006 is the single store of channel preferences and opt-outs, also for phone numbers without an account (decision MSG-ROUTE, BR-TRK-033). Every opt-out or opt-in received on a CHN channel (SMS keywords, push permission) is passed to TRK-006 through IC-TRK-06 UpdatePreference; the keyword is recorded in InboundSms with time and source. Before any CHN send outside TRK-005 (SendReply, SMS command reply) CHN calls IC-TRK-06 CheckAllowed and sends nothing when Blocked; one-time codes are checked by IAM-002 before IC-IAM-01. CHN keeps no opt-out record of its own.

CHN holds no quiet-hours setting: quiet hours are applied by TRK-005 from TRK-006 (BR-TRK-032); they do not apply to sends outside TRK-005 (BR-TRK-026), so one-time codes from IAM-002 (IC-IAM-01) are sent at once.

Agent commission is accrued on payment of an order attributed to an Active network member through the CHK-013 AssistedOrder record (read through IC-CHK-10), and reversed in proportion to refunds, using the rule version in force when the order was paid.

Field records are applied once per client-generated id; a server-side change after download makes the sync of that record a conflict, never a silent overwrite. The field app is one app (decision FIELD-APP): CHN-010 owns its agent functions; its scanning functions are TRK-003 (BR-TRK-011).
Every customer request from any channel becomes a ticket in the help desk through the adapter IC-CRM-01, with its channel recorded; CRM features never write to the licensed plugin tables directly.
Ticket statuses and transitions are those of SM-CRM-01; the adapter maps them to the statuses of the licensed plugin.
Inbound messages are de-duplicated by their channel message ID (for example the e-mail Message-ID); the same message never creates two tickets or two entries.

Messages (decision MSG-ROUTE): notifications about tickets (acknowledgement, status change, resolution with rating link, staff alerts) are sent only through TRK-005 as CRM event codes registered with IC-TRK-04 RegisterEventCode at installation and sent with IC-TRK-04 SendEvent. Agent replies in a conversation the customer started (ticket e-mail reply, WhatsApp, WeChat, chat) are conversational replies and may be sent outside TRK-005 (e-mail reply through the native e-mail account; channels through IC-CHN-04 SendReply), but never to a recipient opted out of that channel in TRK-006, including phone numbers without an account.

Files (decision SINGLE-FILTER): ticket attachment type, size and scanning are checked only by the ADM-008 upload policy for the upload context "ticket attachment" that the CRM plugin registers with ADM-008; CRM keeps only the number of files per ticket. Where attachments are native Download records, downloads through GetFileUpload or Admin DownloadFile are decided by the single SEC-002 filter (BR-SEC-005), to which CRM is a rule provider (ticket customer, staff with Support.Core.Tickets.View).
SLA timers come from SLA policies in the CRM-014 component; a breach marks the subject Breached and runs the escalation action of its level.
Routing rules are evaluated in their configured order; the first match assigns the department; no match assigns the default department.
Internal notes are visible only to staff with ticket permissions; they are excluded from customer pages, customer e-mails and customer data.

Sensitive fields in the 360-degree view are masked unless the user has Support.Core.Customer360.ViewSensitive; every reveal is audited. Support roles do not hold native Customers.CustomersView, because the native customer page shows all fields.
One rating per resolved ticket; ratings are linked to ticket, agent and department and are used only in aggregate on dashboards.
A ready-made answer version is usable only when Approved by a user other than its author; earlier versions are kept.
At most one open fraud referral exists per subject (customer, seller or transaction); new indicators are added to the open referral.

Platform conformance (all CRM features): every new CRM setting key is listed in the CRM plugin key catalogue (key, type, layer, secret flag, default) so pack validation accepts it; keys and fields that hold a credential, key or token (support mailbox credentials, chat account keys) are flagged secret, so the pack loader refuses them and exports omit them. CRM pages, widgets and scheduled tasks run for a store only when IC-PLT-02 IsEnabled(productfeature.<CRM feature ID>) is true for that store. CRM writes go through IRepository<>; if the licensed help desk writes without it, the adapter calls IC-SEC-01 WriteAsync for each change. Business audit events AUD-CRM-nnn are written through IC-SEC-01 with a correlation id.
basis: Proposed (BR-PLT-013, AC-PLT-003-01-04, AC-PLT-022-02-01; BR-SEC-010, BR-SEC-011, BR-SEC-014); CFG-01

rule: When CRM-015 is active, a user in the AccountManager role may impersonate only the customers assigned to that user. CRM-015 supplies this as a rule provider to the single IAM-026 impersonation filter (BR-IAM-130), which also allows Administrators and Agents for customers of their own outlet (IC-IAM-09 provider); CRM has no action filter on Admin CustomerController.Impersonate.

DOC-001 is the only product plugin that overrides IPdfService (DI, INopStartup Order >= 3000; decision OVR-REG; ADM extension register BR-ADM-003). ORD-009 supplies the Invoice and ConsolidatedReceipt document types, their template content and an ORD token provider (IC-ORD-07) through IC-DOC-02; PAY-025 supplies fiscal number and QR through a token provider (IC-DOC-02); other modules add document fields through token providers or native EntityTokensAddedEvent consumers that only add tokens. No other module registers an IPdfService implementation. When no active template exists, the native rendering is used. The override derives from the native PdfService so that the native rendering stays available; in nopCommerce 5.00 PdfService.ResolvePdfFont was replaced by the protected GetFontInfo(pdfSettings, isRtl), which the override uses for the fallback fonts (the IPdfService interface itself is unchanged).
basis: FIT (L1 section 6.2 principle 7; 5.00.1: Libraries/Nop.Services/Common/IPdfService.cs; Libraries/Nop.Services/Common/PdfService.cs:239; EntityTokensAddedEvent); OVR-REG; Proposed

rule: AI-generated drafts (AI-004, AI-009) are Draft documents; they become Final, and can be issued or sent, only after a named person approves them; DOC-001 is the only issuing path.
Every template token must exist in a registered token provider; required tokens without a value stop generation; generated documents are stored in DOC-002.

A document under legal hold (document, entity or type scope) cannot be deleted by any user or by retention; retention disposal of documents is executed by PLT-020 using the document type's retention class.

Document binaries are kept as native Download records; DocumentRecord and DocumentVersion hold the metadata; a customer or vendor can open only own documents. Because the native Nop.Web DownloadController.GetFileUpload and Admin DownloadController.DownloadFile serve any Download by GUID, DOC is a download-access rule provider (IC-SEC-05) to the single SEC-002 ownership filter: it claims the Downloads of DocumentVersion rows and allows them only to the document's customer or vendor and to staff holding Documents.Core.Documents.View; DOC adds no filter of its own on those actions.
basis: FIT (Download; DownloadController.GetFileUpload and Admin DownloadController.DownloadFile have no ownership check); SINGLE-FILTER; Proposed (allowed users)

rule: DOC uploads (vault documents, requirement documents, staff uploads to the repository) are checked by ADM-008 under contexts that DOC registers through IC-ADM-08 (document vault, one context per document requirement, repository upload); DOC endpoints call IC-ADM-08 CheckUpload before storing and keep no file-type or size check of their own. DOC messages are sent through TRK-005: DOC registers its event codes through IC-TRK-04 RegisterEventCode at installation (names Proposed): Documents.Ready, Documents.ReviewRequested, Documents.ReviewDecided, Documents.IntegrityMismatch, Documents.RequirementAlert, Documents.VaultExpiring.
basis: SINGLE-FILTER; MSG-ROUTE; Proposed (context and code names)

rule: Each document version has a SHA-256 hash recorded at creation; verification compares the recomputed hash; watermarks are applied at render or download and never change the stored original.
A document type that requires review becomes Final only after the last reviewer approves; a Final version cannot be edited, only superseded by a new version.

Automatic checks never reject a document for an OCR mismatch or an unreadable field; such documents go to manual review. OCR fields and identity-document checks (AI-005) are suggestions: a staff member decides the outcome (BR-AI-002).

DOC settings are listed in the DOC key catalogue (key, type, layer, secret flag, default); signing-service and OCR-service credentials are flagged secret, so packs refuse them and exports omit them (BR-PLT-013). DOC pages, widgets, scheduled tasks and the IPdfService override check the feature state for the store through IC-PLT-02 before acting; with DOC-001 off the native rendering is used. DOC registers each document type with the PLT-020 retention engine (IC-PLT-08) with the legal-hold check as its hold check.

A government service is a native product of the agency vendor: price = fee; full description = process; each required document = a required FileUpload product attribute; shipping enabled only when the service has a physical output.
Changes to a service affect only applications submitted after the change; submitted applications keep fee, documents and workflow version.
basis: FIT (order item prices stored at placement); Proposed

rule: An application moves out of AwaitingFee only when its order PaymentStatus is Paid (changed only by PAY through IOrderProcessingService); a consumer of OrderPaidEvent starts the move and a scheduled reconciliation task repairs any missed move, because consumer exceptions are swallowed.

Files of e-Government applications are served only to the uploading citizen, users of the owning agency and administrators. EGV enforces this only as a rule provider to the single SEC-002 download ownership filter (GetFileUpload and admin DownloadFile, BR-SEC-005); upload type and size are enforced on the server by ADM-008 under the EGV upload context (BR-ADM-060). EGV registers no upload or download action filter of its own.
basis: REQ-MPC-FR-333; decision SINGLE-FILTER; FIT (GetFileUpload and UploadFileProductAttribute gaps)

rule: An application can be Approved only when every required document is Accepted and every workflow step before approval is complete.
Every decision on a document or application records who, when and the reason (mandatory for reject and resubmission).

An appointment is a CAT-027 direct booking linked to one application; it is created with IC-CAT-07 Book and released with IC-CAT-07 Release; a change is a release and a new booking. CAT enforces slot capacity (BR-CAT-021).

A shipment for an e-Government order line can be created only when its application is Issued. EGV enforces this only as a guard provider (IC-ORD-11) to the ORD-010 shipment-guard host (single IShipmentService.InsertShipmentAsync override and AddShipment action filter, OVR-REG); EGV registers no override or filter of its own for shipments.

A RemittanceLine is created per paid order line of an agency service for the fee amount (delivery fees excluded); refunds before batching reverse the line; refunds after remittance create a negative recovery line.
Remittance reports and batches are per agency; agency users see only their own agency.
Agency users are limited to their own agency by Customer.VendorId; agency administrators can assign only the AgencyOfficer and AgencyAdmin roles and only to users of their own agency.
Every EGV adapter setting that holds a credential, key or token is stored encrypted and flagged secret in the key catalogue, so the pack loader refuses it and exports omit it (BR-PLT-013).

Every EGV page, widget, admin action, callback and scheduled task checks the feature state of the PRD feature it serves through IC-PLT-02 IsEnabled (setting productfeature.<prd-id>, store value else client value) before it runs for a store; when off, nothing is shown and tasks skip that store.

Every new EGV setting key (EgovSettings and adapter settings) is listed in the EGV plugin key catalogue with key, type, layer, secret flag and default, so pack validation accepts it (PLT-003, NFR-X-008). Keys are listed in §10.

EGV sends no message itself. Customer and staff notifications are sent by TRK-005 through IC-TRK-04 SendEvent with event codes EGV registers through IC-TRK-04 RegisterEventCode at installation (names Proposed, listed in BR-TRK-023): Egv.Status.* (application status), Egv.Core.ResubmissionRequested, Egv.Core.ApplicationToReview, Egv.Core.AppointmentConfirmed, Egv.Core.AppointmentChanged, Egv.Core.AppointmentReminder, Egv.Core.FeeNotificationFailed; TRK-006 opt-outs apply. For OrderCompleted.CustomerNotification EGV supplies its order kind through IC-TRK-05; TRK-005 applies the per-client action (BR-TRK-024).
No code is specific to one government service: services differ only by catalogue data, required documents, workflow definition and connector configuration.

The platform shows partner credit, discounting and insurance products as supplied by the partner. It computes no credit score, rate, limit or decision of its own; decisions come only from the partner.

No customer data is sent to a partner without a recorded consent for that partner, purpose and data scope. Only the consented data categories are sent. Consent can be withdrawn; after withdrawal nothing more is sent.

A repayment deduction on a seller settlement never exceeds the instructed amount, the outstanding loan balance or the settlement amount; deductions stop when the loan is Closed or the instruction is Suspended.

Only an open, undisputed, unassigned on-account receivable can be offered for discounting; while Offered or Financed it cannot be offered again. Money received for an Assigned receivable is not paid out to the seller.

When a paid partner service or insurance policy cannot be fulfilled after the configured retries, FIN raises a refund trigger through IC-RET-04 RaiseRefundTrigger with a source type registered in RET (PolicyIssueFailed, PartnerFulfilmentFailed) and the amount paid for it, computed by FIN (RET-005 is the single refund-trigger owner, which calls PAY-016); FIN never calls PAY-016 directly and never changes the order payment status.
basis: Proposed; RET-005 (single refund-trigger owner); FIT (PAY BR-PAY-010)

rule: Insurance claims, their evidence files and partner references are visible only to the policy holder, finance staff and administrators.

A subsidy is applied only while the customer is in the scheme role, the scheme is within its dates and the remaining budget covers the subsidy; refunded or cancelled subsidy amounts return to the budget. The budget is reserved and consumed at placement by the FIN placement participant (IC-CHK-06 Reserve / Confirm / Release) under ILocker key 'fin-scheme-{SchemeId}'.
Partner services are ordinary products: fees and prices, store availability and publication use the native catalogue; FIN adds only the partner link, fulfilment mode and fulfilment record.

Partner credentials are stored encrypted per client instance. Every adapter setting that holds a credential, key or token is flagged secret in the key catalogue, so the pack loader refuses it and exports omit it (BR-PLT-013).

Every FIN page, widget, seller-portal action, callback and scheduled task checks the feature state of the PRD feature it serves through IC-PLT-02 IsEnabled (setting productfeature.<prd-id>, store value else client value) before it runs for a store; when off, nothing is shown and tasks skip that store. Partner-service products (FIN-005) are native products: switching PRD-FIN-005 off does not unpublish them; the administrator unpublishes or unmaps them (AC-FIN-005-04-01).

Every new FIN setting key (FinancialServicesSettings and adapter settings) is listed in the FIN plugin key catalogue with key, type, layer, secret flag and default, so pack validation accepts it (PLT-003, NFR-X-008). Keys are listed in §10.

Every FIN notification (referral status, repayment deducted, invoice financed or declined, policy issued or failed, claim status, partner fulfilment completed or failed) is sent by TRK-005 through IC-TRK-04 SendEvent; FIN registers its event codes with IC-TRK-04 RegisterEventCode at installation (names Proposed, listed in BR-TRK-023: Fin.Core.ReferralStatusChanged, Fin.Core.RepaymentDeducted, Fin.Core.InvoiceFinancingDecided, Fin.Core.PolicyIssued, Fin.Core.PolicyIssueFailed, Fin.Core.ClaimStatusChanged, Fin.Core.PartnerFulfilmentCompleted, Fin.Core.PartnerFulfilmentFailed) and sends no message itself; customer opt-outs (TRK-006) apply.

The registration type (CustomerSettings.UserRegistrationType: Standard, EmailValidation, AdminApproval, Disabled) is one value for the installation. Trade-account approval does not use AdminApproval; it uses the IAM-023 queue so that retail registration stays open.
basis: FIT (UserRegistrationType; setting saved without store scope)

rule: Identifiers: an email address belongs to at most one customer (native check). A normalised mobile number belongs to at most one customer (unique index on the IAM PhoneIdentity table; the native 5.00 check refuses only a number already verified on another account). One customer may hold both.

Block lists: registration and login POSTs (native CustomerController.Register and Login, and the IAM plugin mobile registration and mobile login POST actions) are checked against SEL-013 Block entries with scope registration, login or all by the Platform core action filter owned by SEL-013. IAM keeps no block list of its own and adds no second filter.
Mobile numbers are stored in international format; a number entered without the international prefix gets the calling code of the store default country.

Mobile identity: login by mobile number and code is native in nopCommerce 5.00 (OtpSettings.LoginByPhoneEnabled, ValidateCustomerByPhoneAsync) and is not rebuilt. DI overrides registered in the IAM plugin INopStartup with Order >= 3000 remain for what 5.00 does not do: ICustomerRegistrationService (RegisterCustomerAsync accepts a verified mobile number without email; the subclass inherits the new ValidateCustomerByPhoneAsync unchanged) and IAuthenticationService (adds a customer GUID claim at sign-in and resolves it, so customers without email are found, and applies the session checks of BR-IAM-040). Reason: native RegisterCustomerAsync rejects an empty email and password, and CookieAuthenticationService resolves customers only by the email or username claim. Only the IAM plugin overrides these two interfaces (DI-override register).

One-time codes are random, single-use, bound to one purpose (register, login, recover, confirm change, assisted consent, MFA), stored only as a hash, and never logged in clear. Validity, length, maximum attempts, resend interval and send limits per number are the native OtpSettings values (OtpTimeLife, OtpLength, OtpFailedAllowedAttempts, OtpCountAttemptsToSendCode, OtpTimeToRepeat; defaults not stated); the limit per IP address is an IAM setting (default not stated). Failed attempts on IAM codes count towards the native lockout (FailedLoginAttempts); native login codes are locked by the native OTP counter instead.

Native code login (5.00) does not check the password lockout or MFA: an IAM global action filter on the native code-verification action refuses sign-in for a customer whose CannotLoginUntilDateUtc is in the future, and for members of MFA-required or sensitive roles requires the password step and the second factor (BR-IAM-030, BR-IAM-020).

For accounts holding a role listed as sensitive, password recovery by email link or SMS code alone is not allowed: an IAM global action filter on CustomerController.PasswordRecoverySend [POST] stops the native token, opens a recovery request and shows the same neutral message as for other accounts; the request needs the configured extra check (security questions with hashed answers, or confirmation by a second user holding Customers.CustomersCreateEditDelete who is not the requester).
Password rules use only the native CustomerSettings values (length, complexity, reuse, lifetime, lockout, recovery link validity); no second password policy is built.

MFA by role: the setting "MFA-required roles" lists role system names. An IAM global action filter redirects a signed-in member of such a role without a selected provider to the native MFA settings page (exempt: that page, logout, policy pages, static files). MultiFactorAuthenticationSettings.ForceMultifactorAuthentication stays off, because it would force every holder of Security.EnableMultiFactorAuthentication, including Registered. Members of MFA-required roles cannot remove their own provider. For single sign-on, the identity provider must assert a multi-factor method, else the IAM second factor is requested (Proposed).

Second factors are IMultiFactorAuthenticationMethod plugins following the bundled GoogleAuthenticator pattern: the verification component posts to the plugin controller, which reads CustomerMultiFactorAuthenticationInfo from the session and calls SignInCustomerAsync only after a successful check. Email-code, SMS-code and hardware-key providers are built; GoogleAuthenticator is reused (still the only bundled provider in 5.00.1). The SMS-code provider sends through IC-IAM-01, which delivers through the native 5.00 ISmsService and the active ISmsProvider.

Sessions: every sign-in creates a UserSession record (session id claim, customer, created, last activity, IP address, user agent). The IAuthenticationService override (BR-IAM-011) rejects a request whose session is revoked, expired by the idle timeout of the user class, or over the concurrent-session limit. Forced logout revokes all sessions and sets Customer.RequireReLogin; the native next successful login clears RequireReLogin. Session changes for one customer run under ILocker key 'iam-session-{CustomerId}'.
basis: REQ-MPC-FR-013; FIT (Customer.RequireReLogin; ValidateCustomerAsync resets it); Proposed

rule: Product role catalogue (role system names, Proposed; the modules that use each name as a default role or actor role are in brackets, checked over all 24 content files). Staff roles: Finance (CHK, CHN, EGV, FIN, INT, INV, LOG, MKT, PAY, RET, RPT, SEL, SVC), Risk (AI, CRM, ORD, PAY, SEL), Agent (IAM-026; CHK, CHN, CRM, EGV, LOG, PAY, RET, RPT, SVC, TRK), Auditor (IAM, SEC; ADM, CAT, DOC, INV, PLT, RPT), SecurityOfficer (IAM, SEC), PrivacyOfficer (IAM, SEC), Operations (ADM, SVC), OperationsManager (RPT), Compliance (ADM, DOC, SEL), PlatformOperator (ADM, PLT), Support and SupportManager (IAM, CRM, RET, RPT; Support also INV, TRK), AccountManager (CRM), AgencyOfficer and AgencyAdmin (EGV), Programme (FIN), Stock and Quality (INV), Warehouse (INV, LOG, RET, RPT), LogisticsOps and Courier (LOG, TRK), Marketing (MKT, RPT, SRC), Content and ContentApprover (MKT), Catalogue (SRC), Analyst (RPT), Procurement (SEL). Customer roles: TradeBuyer (IAM-023; LOG, PAY); one system customer role per company, generated by CAT-040 for company assortments, with system name CompanyAssortment-{CompanyId} (Proposed by CAT-040). Native roles are unchanged and keep their native system names: Administrators, Registered, Guests, Vendors; ForumModerators exists only when the bundled Misc.Forums plugin is installed (5.00 moved it out of core: ForumDefaults.ForumModeratorsRoleName); seller staff are Vendors members, never a separate admin role (BR-SEL-010). Company roles buyer, approver and company administrator are not nopCommerce roles (BR-IAM-120). Every module uses exactly these names as default roles. The IAM plugin creates every missing catalogue role at install and at every application start (AC-IAM-007-04-01); no module relies on native start-up to create a role, because PermissionService creates a missing role only when it installs a new permission. A name used by a module and missing here is a defect (T-IAM-12). Client-specific roles (for example the ORD order-intervention approver, KTDA sales, export and legal roles) are configuration only.
basis: Proposed; owner decisions Role system names and Roles; FIT (PermissionService.InsertPermissionsAsync)

rule: Effective permissions are the union of the permissions of all roles of the user, plus active delegations (IAM-009), limited by the user scopes (IAM-008). There are no deny rules.

Role and permission packs use 5.00 permission system names (news, polls and forums permissions are the plugin names News.*, Polls.*, Forums.*); an unknown name is an error in pack validation (IC-PLT-01 Validate) and grants nothing, because native InsertPermissionMappingAsync would skip it without error.

Role packs: native permissions that a module gives to a product role are declared in that module chapter and mapped by the role pack (PLT-003, IC-PLT-01 Apply through IPermissionService.InsertPermissionMappingAsync); native default mappings are not removed by a pack unless the pack names the removal. Examples: Customers.CustomersImpersonation and Security.AccessAdminPanel to Agent (CHK-013) and to AccountManager (CRM-015); Security.AccessAdminPanel, Catalog.ProductsView and Orders.OrdersView to AgencyOfficer and AgencyAdmin, and shipment permissions to AgencyOfficer only (EGV-006); native Promotions, ContentManagement and Orders.GiftCards permissions to Marketing and Content (MKT).

Permission exclusions declared by modules are checked when a pack is validated (IC-PLT-01) and when a mapping is saved in SecurityController.PermissionEditPopup [POST] (IAM action filter): Vendors never hold Orders.ReturnRequestsView or Orders.ReturnRequestsCreateEditDelete (RET); Support and SupportManager never hold Customers.CustomersView (BR-CRM-030). Customer-to-role assignments that break BR-SEL-010 (a seller staff user in a non-Vendors admin role) are SEL checks, not IAM checks.

Scopes (dimension store, region, outlet, category, value band or time window; values) are assigned per user or role and per permission. List queries in the admin area filter by scope (registered core modification, L1 §6.3); single-record actions are checked by an IAM action filter; permission checks with scopes and delegations go through the single IAM override of IPermissionService (also used by SEC-010 time-bound grants). The outlet scope of an agent comes from the IAM-026 outlet assignment. A value-band scope on an approval permission is the authority limit read by ADM-006 through IC-IAM-06.

Delegation: a user can delegate only a permission they hold and that is marked delegable; it has a start and an end; it cannot be delegated again; segregation-of-duties rules (for example BR-PAY-080) still apply to the delegate.

Read-access logging: an IAM global action filter on admin actions that display one customer personal data (Customer Edit, Order Edit, customer address edit; the full list is fixed at build start) writes AUD-IAM-010 with staff user, customer and page.

Deactivation (by the customer or by staff) keeps all data and stops sign-in and marketing; deletion with anonymisation is only through IAM-017. Self-reactivation is allowed only after self-deactivation.
Authentication events are append-only: the IAM plugin offers no edit or delete, and every event is copied to the SEC-004 audit trail.

Policy acceptance is recorded only by IAM (IC-IAM-05), per policy system name and version, for a customer and, for seller terms, the vendor (SEL-006 records through IC-IAM-05). The version and the "re-acceptance required" flag are those of the MKT-008 Effective version returned by IC-MKT-03; IAM stores no policy text, no version and no flag of its own. When the Effective version has the flag set, an IAM global action filter redirects signed-in users (and seller owners in the seller portal) who have not accepted it to the acceptance page (exempt: logout, policy pages, the acceptance page, static files).
basis: REQ-MPC-FR-006; owner decision Terms and consent records; Proposed

rule: Erasure completeness: the IAM override of IGdprService.PermanentDeleteCustomerAsync calls the native method and also clears Customer.FirstName, LastName, Gender, DateOfBirth, Company, StreetAddress, StreetAddress2, ZipPostalCode, City, County, Phone (and PhoneSmsVerified), Fax, VatNumber, CustomCustomerAttributesXML, LastIpAddress and AdminComment, and the personal data in IAM plugin tables (phone identity, sessions, verification results, preferences), and calls every erasure provider registered through IC-IAM-08; the request completes only when all providers report Erased. Orders, invoices and their addresses are kept or anonymised under the retention rules (PLT-020, SEC-012). In 5.00 the native method also deletes the cart and all custom wishlists, and private messages sent and received; news comments and forum data are deleted by the Misc.News and Misc.Forums plugins on CustomerPermanentlyDeleted, so IAM does not handle them.
basis: FIT (GdprService.PermanentDeleteCustomerAsync clears only Email, EmailToRevalidate, Username; ignores orders and ActivityLog — Libraries/Nop.Services/Gdpr/GdprService.cs:258-351; Plugins/Nop.Plugin.Misc.News/Services/Events/EventConsumer.cs:69); VER-500

rule: Every privacy request (staff export, correction, deletion) gets a due date from the country profile (SEC-012); an open request past its due date is Overdue.
basis: Inference from REQ-KTDA-LEG-001 (law names inference, DP-01)

rule: Account synchronisation uses the single INT-004 outbox (IntegrationMessage, SM-INT-01): IAM event consumers only write outbox messages with channel "account sync" through IC-INT-09 Enqueue; the INT delivery task sends them through the IC-IAM-03 adapter with the INT-004 retry and dead-letter policy; IAM keeps no outbox, retry state or queue view of its own. Inbound changes update only configured fields; the system of record per field is configuration.
Identity verification stores the result, adapter, reference, time and the fields matched, not identity document images; results are kept under the retention rules (PLT-020).

Company membership and company roles (buyer, approver, company administrator) are kept in IAM plugin tables per company, not as nopCommerce customer roles; the nopCommerce role TradeBuyer marks an approved trade buyer and drives trade prices and ACL. Other modules read the company of a customer through IC-IAM-07; CAT-040 per-company system roles are allowed and are kept in step through the IC-IAM-07 membership provider; approval thresholds per company role are stored by CHK-018.

Where TaxSettings.EuVatEnabled is switched on to record VAT numbers, EuVatUseWebService and EuVatAllowVatExemption stay off and Country.SubjectToVat is set deliberately for every country, because native IsVatExemptAsync exempts addresses in countries not subject to VAT.

Assisted service and acting sessions: each agent has a personal account (never shared) and at least one assigned outlet. The acting session is the native impersonation (Admin CustomerController.Impersonate, used by CHK-013 and CRM-015), so native order notes record the actor. The action carries ONE product filter, owned by IAM-026 (owner decision): a global action filter matched on the method name Impersonate (the route action name is Edit), running after the native CheckPermission authorization filter (Customers.CustomersImpersonation). It allows members of Administrators; for every other user it calls every registered rule provider (IC-IAM-09) and allows the request when at least one provider returns Allow; otherwise it refuses with the message key of the first Deny, else Iam.ImpersonationNotAllowed, and writes AUD-IAM-019. Providers: the IAM-026 agent rule (holders of Identity.Core.AssistedService.Access: the agent has an assigned outlet, the customer is not staff, the customer is registered at one of the agent outlets, and the customer code is given where the setting requires it) and the CRM-015 account-manager rule (the user is the assigned account manager of the customer). A provider whose feature is off for the store (IC-PLT-02) returns NotApplicable. The native checks of the action (inactive customer, non-administrator acting for an administrator) still apply. No other module adds a filter to this action. Registrations by an agent are stamped with agent and outlet (AssistedServiceRecord); the order link with agent and outlet is the CHK-013 AssistedOrder record.
basis: REQ-MPC-FR-014; REQ-MPC-FR-025; owner decision Impersonation filters; FIT (CustomerController.Impersonate; CheckPermissionAttribute is an authorization filter; WebWorkContext; OrderProcessingService)

rule: Key catalogue: every new IAM setting key is listed in the IAM plugin key catalogue with key, type, layer, secret flag and default (NFR-X-008); keys that hold a credential, key or token (identity-provider client secrets, verification adapter credentials, synchronisation endpoint credentials, SMS gateway credentials if held by IAM) are flagged secret, so packs refuse them and exports omit them (BR-PLT-013).

Feature state: IAM features that are not always on (IAM-005, IAM-009, IAM-013, IAM-022, IAM-023, IAM-025, IAM-026, IAM-027) check IC-PLT-02 IsEnabled for the store before showing pages or widgets, running filters or scheduled work; the core identity features are always on.

Messages: IAM notifications (welcome and validation emails, invitation, new-country login, trade decision, privacy-request updates, deactivation and reactivation) are sent by TRK-005: native templates through IWorkflowMessageService (TRK-005 override) and IAM templates through the TRK-005 engine (IAM registers them through IC-TRK-04 RegisterEventCode at installation; names Proposed, listed in BR-TRK-023: Iam.NewCountryLogin.CustomerNotification, Iam.Invitation.Email, Iam.TradeApplicationApproved.CustomerNotification, Iam.Core.TradeApplicationRejected, Iam.Core.MobileRegistrationCompleted, Iam.Core.SuspiciousLogin, Iam.Core.AccessReviewOpened, Iam.Core.AccessReviewOverdue, Iam.Core.PolicyAcceptanceRequired, Iam.Core.PrivacyRequestUpdated, Iam.Core.AccountDeactivated, Iam.Core.AccountReactivated). One-time codes are the only IAM messages sent outside TRK-005: IAM calls CHN-005 directly (IC-IAM-01, owner decision). Before sending a code IAM calls IC-TRK-06 CheckAllowed (category Security codes) and sends nothing when TRK answers Blocked; an opted-out number (also one without an account) gets a code only if the client marks Security codes mandatory (BR-TRK-031, BR-TRK-026). Quiet hours and message limits do not apply to codes. Delivery results of codes stay in the IAM OtpChallenge and the CHN-005 log.
basis: Proposed; owner decision Messages outside TRK (MSG-ROUTE); BR-TRK-026

rule: Data written through the API or an adapter goes through the native nopCommerce service interfaces (for example IProductService, ICustomerService, IShipmentService, IOrderProcessingService), and so through the override that OVR-REG assigns to each (IProductService CAT-002, IOrderProcessingService CHK-003, IShipmentService.InsertShipmentAsync ORD-010); no adapter or endpoint writes core tables directly or changes order, payment or shipment status outside the service methods; INT registers no service override of its own. An INT endpoint or adapter that inserts a shipment for an order with lot- or serial-tracked lines calls INV IC-INV-07 Capture and Confirm around the insert (BR-INV-070; Proposed); the scope catalogue (BR-INT-006) has no shipment-creation scope today.

Every INT setting key is listed in the INT plugin key catalogue (key, type, layer, secret flag, default) so pack validation accepts it; INT keeps credentials, keys and secrets only in encrypted plugin-table fields (ConnectorConfig.CredentialsRef, WebhookSubscription.SecretRef, ApiClient.KeyHash), never in settings, and any setting that would hold one is flagged secret. INT pages, consumers and scheduled tasks act for a store only when IC-PLT-02 IsEnabled returns true for the INT feature concerned.
API access is denied by default: an API client has explicit scopes and store limits; every call outside them returns 403 and is logged.

API scope catalogue (names Proposed; owner INT-001): products.read (catalogue read, used by CAT-011 IC-CAT-01), products.read.unpublished (CAT-011 staff clients: unpublished listings as well), products.write, orders.read, search.read (SRC-024 search API for channel systems), payments.notify (PAY-005 bank notifications), shipments.write (TRK-002 tracking events), documents.read, webhooks.manage. A module that needs a new scope adds it to this catalogue; a scope outside the catalogue cannot be granted.

API versions: a published version never changes incompatibly; incompatible changes go to a new major version; a deprecated version keeps working for the deprecation window and announces its retirement date in every response and in the change log (SM-INT-05).
Rate limits apply per API client (gateway or INT plugin); the native global limiter (CommonConfig.PermitLimit, off by default) is not a per-client limit.

Event consumers only write an IntegrationMessage (outbox); delivery and adapter calls run in scheduled tasks, never inside the consumer (consumer exceptions are swallowed by the native event publisher).
A seller's subscription receives only events of orders that contain the seller's items, and only those lines.
Webhook URLs are https only; every delivery is signed with the subscription secret and carries a message id and timestamp.
Delivery is at least once: retries keep the message id; receivers de-duplicate by message id; no message is deleted before it is Delivered or Discarded by a person.
Transient errors are retried under the policy; permanent errors go to dead letter at once; replay and discard need a reason and are audited.

One outbox: every outbound message the product sends to an external system is an IntegrationMessage, written by INT or by another module through IC-INT-09 Enqueue, and follows the INT-004 retry, dead-letter and replay rules. Callers: IAM-019 (account sync, BR-IAM-100) and INV-012 (stock sync, BR-INV-090).

For each entity type exchanged with an external system, one master of record is configured per client (external system or nopCommerce); only changes from the master are applied; changes to a field mastered elsewhere are not sent and are replaced at the next sync.
basis: D ("in step in both directions"); Proposed

rule: Postings and sync exchanges are idempotent per external key: a repeated posting or record with the same key is not applied twice.
A SAGE 200 posting batch is final only when SAGE 200 acknowledges it; a period is Reconciled only when no exception is open.

INT adapter operations that workflow steps may call are registered in the ADM-002 step-operation catalogue through IC-ADM-01 RegisterStepOperation (ADM owns the catalogue); INT runs them only on active adapters, logs each call with the correlation id in the IntegrationMessage log, and leaves timeout and retry to the calling step.

PostGlobal is a TRK-002 tracking source: the INT-007 adapter submits PostGlobal events through IC-TRK-01 and TRK-002 maps them with its SourceCodeMapping; INT keeps no status map of its own; unmapped codes are rejected by TRK-002 and send no customer notification.

Tracking numbers returned by PostGlobal are written through IShipmentService.UpdateShipmentAsync; shipment shipped and delivered states change only through IOrderProcessingService.ShipAsync / DeliverAsync.
Submissions to government systems are sent only after approval by a second person holding Integrations.Core.GovSubmissions.Approve.

Stock quantities change only through the native IProductService inventory methods (AdjustInventoryAsync, BookReservedInventoryAsync, ReverseBookedInventoryAsync, UpdateProductWarehouseInventoryAsync with AddStockQuantityHistoryEntryAsync) called by native order flows or by the INV adjustment service (IC-INV-01); every change writes a StockQuantityHistory entry. No product code sets Product.StockQuantity, ProductWarehouseInventory.StockQuantity or ProductAttributeCombination.StockQuantity directly.

Every INV page, widget, action filter, provider (IC-INV-04, IC-CHK-01) and scheduled task checks the state of its feature for the store through IC-PLT-02 (setting productfeature.<prd-id>, store then shared value) before it acts; when the feature is off the provider returns no change and native behaviour applies. Every new INV setting key is listed in the INV key catalogue (key, type, layer, secret flag, default); keys that hold a credential, key or token are flagged secret (BR-PLT-013, CFG-01).
