All INV plugin tables are written through IRepository<>, so the SEC decorator captures old and new values (BR-SEC-010); INV writes no data through INopDataProvider directly. Business events AUD-INV-nnn are written through IC-SEC-01 IAuditTrail.WriteAsync with the request correlation id (BR-SEC-014).
Every warehouse has a code, unique in the installation, and latitude and longitude; they are stored in the WarehouseExtension plugin table, not in the native Warehouse or Address tables.
basis: D; Proposed (uniqueness); FIT (Warehouse and Address have no code or coordinates)

rule: INV-004 owns the unpaid-order timeout, reminders and release for every payment method. Stock is decremented at order placement (native). For each payment method the client sets a payment window, a reminder count and interval, and an expiry action Remind, Flag or Cancel (all defaults not stated); orders whose payment method has no window are never processed. When the window expires and the action is Cancel, INV-004 cancels only if, under ILocker key 'pay-order-{OrderId}', the order PaymentStatus is still Pending and no PaymentTransaction for the order is Successful or Authorized (IC-INV-02), and the order has no shipment (Proposed); it calls IOrderProcessingService.CancelOrderAsync(order, notifyCustomer: true), which returns the stock (the call reaches the CHK-003 IOrderProcessingService override, OVR-REG). CancelOrderAsync does not void or refund payments; a payment that succeeds after the cancellation is handled by PAY (SuccessfulAfterCancel); INV raises no refund trigger (refund triggers: RET-005).

A hold never changes native stock. Stock available to a customer = GetTotalStockQuantityAsync (with the IC-INV-04 lot rules) - active holds of other customers. The check is an IC-CHK-01 cart check provider called by the CHK-003 IShoppingCartService override (BR-CHK-015, decision OVR-REG); INV overrides no cart method. When the native stock check passes but other customers' holds make the quantity unavailable, INV adds Inv.HeldByOthers; when the native check already produced ShoppingCart.OutOfStock or ShoppingCart.QuantityExceedsStock and other customers hold the product, INV, as the registered replacer of those two warnings, replaces that warning with Inv.HeldByOthers and the hold-adjusted quantity. Holds are created or renewed by an EntityInsertedEvent / EntityUpdatedEvent<ShoppingCartItem> consumer (cart) and an action filter on checkout start; a failed consumer only means no hold. A hold is active until its expiry time; expired holds are ignored even before the release task runs. Holds become Converted on order placement, or Released on expiry, removal from the cart (EntityDeletedEvent<ShoppingCartItem>) or a Listing.Withdrawn release job.
basis: D; FC-M26-002; FC-M03-005; OVR-REG; FIT (ShoppingCartService.cs:1141, 1648, 1706); Proposed (formula, consumers)

rule: At most the configured number of reminders is sent per order, at the configured interval; none is sent once the order is paid, authorised or cancelled.

Native 5.00 unpaid-order functions stay off while INV-004 owns the unpaid-order timeout and reminders: OrderSettings.AutoCancelEnabled false and ReminderSettings.PendingOrdersEnabled false in every store; the pack validation (PLT-003) refuses a pack that switches either on for a client that uses INV-004.
basis: INV-HOLD; FIT (AutoCancelOrdersTask.cs:56-122; ProcessPendingOrdersTask.cs:54-164); Proposed (pack validation); VER-500

rule: Native admin pages that change a stock quantity are intercepted by a global IAsyncActionFilter registered by the INV plugin for Admin ProductController.Edit [POST], BulkEditSave [POST], ProductAttributeCombinationEditPopup [POST], ProductAttributeCombinationCreatePopup [POST] and ImportExcel [POST]. A post that changes a stock quantity (product, warehouse or combination) is refused before the action runs, with message Inv.UseStockAdjustment; ImportExcel is allowed only with Inventory.Core.Adjustments.Approve. Native order flows (placement, cancellation, shipment, order edit, deletion) are not intercepted. The native return-request edit (ReturnedQuantity, which adjusts stock) is intercepted by RET (BR-RET-001), not by INV. Every INV action filter is listed in the ADM extension register (BR-ADM-001). A ModelReceivedEvent veto is not used because BulkEditSave and ImportExcel do not check ModelState.
basis: FIT (ProductController.cs:983, 1227, 3061, 3887, 4047; 5.00.1 bulk edit sets StockQuantity with no history entry, ProductController.cs:4382)

rule: Every INV movement writes a stock history message in the form "<document type> <document reference> <reason code>" (Proposed) and an INV record that holds the user, time, reason, note and document.

After an INV movement the INV service applies the same rules as native AdjustInventoryAsync: LowStockActivity against MinStockQuantity, QuantityBelow store-owner and vendor emails when the change lowers stock below NotifyAdminForQuantityBelow, and back-in-stock notifications when available stock rises from 0 or below to above 0.

An adjustment whose size is above the approval threshold needs approval by a user with Inventory.Core.Adjustments.Approve who is not the requester. Document-backed movements (receipt, transfer, count posting below the threshold, ERP sync, RET-004 return restock) do not need a separate approval.

For a product that uses multiple warehouses, an INV movement changes ProductWarehouseInventory.StockQuantity of the named warehouse through UpdateProductWarehouseInventoryAsync and writes AddStockQuantityHistoryEntryAsync for that warehouse; it never calls AdjustInventoryAsync, which for such products changes ReservedQuantity and spreads the quantity over warehouses.
A receipt adds only accepted quantities to stock; shortages, damaged units, failed inspection and over-receipts are discrepancies; a receipt above the open quantity plus tolerance is refused.
Transfer dispatch lowers the source warehouse; in-transit units are available nowhere; receipt raises the destination warehouse; a shortfall becomes an adjustment request with reason Lost in transit.
Count variance = counted quantity - (system quantity at count creation + net movements in stock history since then); variances are posted as adjustments with reason Count variance under BR-INV-033.

Lots are recorded for products with ManageInventoryMethod ManageStock only. Lot quantity rises at receipt and falls at shipment, disposal or adjustment. Shipment allocation is captured through IC-INV-07 (Capture before the shipment insert, Confirm after the shipment items are saved, Cancel when the insert is refused or fails), called by the INV filter on Admin OrderController.AddShipment [POST] and by every LOG shipment path (BR-LOG-003); a lot quantity or serial number in an open capture cannot be captured again; captures run under ILocker key 'inv-product-{ProductId}'. A shipment item of a tracked product saved without a confirmed capture is a capture exception. Per warehouse, sum of lot quantities = native stock + quantity placed but not yet shipped; differences are exceptions. Only Released lots can be shipped.

Unsellable lot statuses are Quarantine, Blocked, Expired and Recalled. The INV sellable-stock provider (IC-INV-04), called by the CAT-002 IProductService override of GetTotalStockQuantityAsync (decision OVR-REG), subtracts the quantity of unsellable lots (per warehouse when a warehouse is given); INV does not override IProductService. Shipment lot selection is pre-filled by FEFO: earliest expiry first, then earliest receipt.
Serial-tracked products need exactly one distinct serial number per unit at receipt and at shipment; a serial number is unique per product.

INV-012 runs on the INT-005 framework (IC-INT-03). Inbound sync messages are applied once per external message ID (BR-INT-021); the master of record is set per data type (stock level, movement, purchase order, valuation) as BR-INT-020 defines; every inbound stock change is posted through IC-INV-01 (BR-INV-001, BR-INV-034), never by writing stock fields; outbound messages are written to the single INT-004 outbox through IC-INT-09 Enqueue (channel stock sync) and follow the INT-004 retry, dead-letter and replay rules (SM-INT-01, BR-INT-015); INV keeps a record of applied inbound message IDs and the conflict list only, and no outbound queue, retry state or dead-letter state of its own.
basis: (BR-INT-020, BR-INT-021, IC-INT-03); BR-INT-015 (one outbox); Proposed; NFR-X-007

rule: Units sold count order lines of orders placed in the period, excluding cancelled orders; sellable stock is GetTotalStockQuantityAsync (including BR-INV-071); a daily snapshot of sellable stock per product and warehouse is taken by a scheduled task. Snapshots and movements by reason are read by RPT-001 through IC-INV-06 (decision ANL-002-OWN); INV-013 does not report fast and slow movers or stock levels itself.

Native shipment state changes only through IOrderProcessingService.ShipAsync (not for pickup orders), ReadyForPickupAsync (pickup orders only) and DeliverAsync; code never sets Shipment.ShippedDateUtc, ReadyForPickupDateUtc, DeliveryDateUtc or Order.ShippingStatusId directly. Each call is made at most once per shipment and state, under ILocker key 'shipment-{ShipmentId}' (shared with TRK), after re-reading the shipment. IOrderProcessingService is overridden by CHK-003 only (OVR-REG); if that override refuses the call through an ORD hook (for example an ORD-010 hold), the LOG step keeps its state and shows the refusal message.
basis: FIT (OrderProcessingService.ShipAsync, ReadyForPickupAsync, DeliverAsync throw if already set); OVR-REG

rule: LOG creates native shipments only through IShipmentService.InsertShipmentAsync, never through the repository, so the single override hosted by ORD-010 (OVR-REG) runs every shipment guard provider registered through IC-ORD-11 (PAY letter of credit, ORD-010 hold, EGV-004 issue check). For lot- or serial-tracked lines on every LOG path (fulfilment screens, IC-LOG-07, APIs) LOG calls IC-INV-07 Capture before the insert, Confirm after the shipment items are saved, and Cancel when a guard refuses or the insert fails (BR-INV-070, BR-INV-080); Admin OrderController.AddShipment is covered by the INV action filter. A refusal or a refused capture saves nothing. LOG registers no override of IShipmentService.

A shipping option is shown only if its rate method is active (ShippingSettings.ActiveShippingRateComputationMethodSystemNames), the shipping method is allowed for the destination country (ShippingMethodCountryMapping) and serviceability allows it (BR-LOG-020).

Delivery fee = sum of the components defined for the service level in the fee-table version in force: base by zone or distance band, weight band, location type (rural / urban), pickup or delivery; each component is kept for the breakdown; amounts are rounded per component to the currency minor unit and the fee is the sum of the rounded components.

Distance bands use the straight-line distance between origin and destination coordinates (origin warehouse coordinates read through IC-INV-05 GetWarehouseLocation; destination LOG-015 AddressGeo). If either has no coordinates, the zone table of the same service level applies; if there is no zone table, the option is not offered and the case is logged.
Fee tables, pickup fees and partner share rules are versioned with an effective date; an order keeps the versions in force when it was quoted and placed.
Partner revenue share per partner and service level is fixed or a percentage of the delivery fee; partner share + client share = delivery fee; recorded per shipment at partner assignment.
LOG-002 owns delivery and pickup fee tables; COD fees are PAY-015; payment-method fees are PAY-015.

Delivery for a service level is offered only if the destination is in a coverage area allowing that level, with the Marketplace pack in the coverage of every seller of the (sub-)order, and, where a product of the (sub-)order has a ProductDeliveryOption list, in that list; pickup is offered only at outlets serving the destination area that are not closed on the expected arrival date, not flagged full and, where a list exists, allowed for every product. IC-LOG-06 IsServiceable and GetOutlets apply the same rule for other modules.
basis: REQ-MPC-FR-197; REQ-MPC-FR-069; REQ-MPC-FR-188; Proposed (product list, EGV-004)

rule: Location type (rural / urban) is an attribute of the coverage area (Proposed). LOG-002 fees and PAY routing and COD fee rules read it from there; there is one source.

EDT: dispatch day = order day if before the ORD-011 cut-off of the service level on a working day of the ORD-011 calendar, else the next working day; then moved to the next departure day of the transport link; earliest = dispatch day + ORD-011 handling time + minimum transit days, latest = dispatch day + ORD-011 handling time + maximum transit days, skipping non-working days of the ORD-011 calendar. The range is stored with the order as the promise. Cut-off, handling time and calendar have one source, ORD-011 ServiceLevel.

Carrier assignment rules are evaluated by priority on destination area, service level, weight band, seller, fulfilment model and special handling (cold chain, hazardous); optional rate shopping picks the cheapest quote among eligible carriers; with no match the default carrier applies; manual override needs a reason.

One active booking per shipment or return shipment; every booking request carries the idempotency key ShipmentId (or ReturnShipmentId) + attempt; reassignment cancels the active booking first. LOG returns the tracking reference of a return booking to RET-003, which registers it with TRK-002 (IC-TRK-01 RegisterExternalReference); LOG registers no reference itself.

Tracker resolution: every product shipping-rate method (LOG fee engine, carrier adapters, postal service levels) and the LOG outlet provider return the TRK-002 hub tracker from GetShipmentTrackerAsync. IShipmentService.GetShipmentTrackerAsync is not overridden, because IShipmentService has one owner (ORD-010, OVR-REG); PostGlobal events reach the hub through INT-007, so no PostGlobal tracker is needed on shipment pages.

S10 identifiers follow the UPU S10 format (service indicator, serial, check digit, ISO country code). Serials are taken in order from the configured range under ILocker key 'log-s10-{series}', stored with a unique index, and never reused. Entered or received S10 numbers are validated for format and check digit.
Fulfilment model per order line: product setting, else seller opt-in (SEL-018), else client default; values merchant-fulfilled, client-fulfilled, third-party.

Nearest warehouse: among warehouses with enough stock for the line (ProductWarehouseInventory), the one with the shortest straight-line distance to the destination (warehouse coordinates through IC-INV-05 GetWarehouseLocation; a warehouse without coordinates is not a candidate for distance); ties go to the lowest warehouse Id.
A package can be confirmed packed only when every picked item and quantity matches the order lines of the task; dispatch requires a carrier or route assignment and a tracking reference.

Each service level has a set of accepted proof methods (signature, OTP, QR scan, courier confirmation, staff confirmation). DeliverAsync is called only after a POD record of an accepted method exists for the shipment.

A home-delivery OTP generated by LOG-012 is valid only for its shipment, is single-use, and is locked after the configured number of wrong attempts. Pickup codes and QR codes are CHK-012 (BR-CHK-016); LOG calls IC-CHK-09 Verify and acts only on Valid, and calls IC-CHK-09 MarkUsed after DeliverAsync succeeds.

Files that LOG receives (proof-of-delivery media from outlet and courier pages, carriers and IC-LOG-04; delivery exception evidence; manually uploaded carrier labels) belong to the LOG upload contexts "proof-of-delivery media", "delivery exception evidence" and "carrier label", which LOG registers at installation through IC-ADM-08 RegisterUploadContext as own-endpoint contexts; each file is checked through IC-ADM-08 CheckUpload (type, size, signature, scan) before it is stored with IDownloadService.InsertDownloadAsync, because the ADM-008 IDownloadService backstop sees only IFormFile uploads. LOG keeps no type or size check of its own. LOG implements a download-access rule provider (IC-SEC-05) that claims proof-of-delivery media (ProofOfDelivery.MediaDownloadIds) and allows them on admin DownloadFile only to holders of Logistics.Core.ProofOfDelivery.View; LOG registers no download filter.
basis: SINGLE-FILTER; IC-ADM-08; IC-SEC-05; FIT (DownloadService.InsertDownloadAsync takes bytes, GetDownloadBitsAsync takes IFormFile; Admin DownloadController.DownloadFile has only AuthorizeAdmin); Proposed (context names)

rule: Delivery exception reason codes are a configurable list (initial values from source: unreachable, not at home, address issue, refused; incident types lost, damaged, delayed). After the configured maximum of failed attempts the action is return to sender. An exception open beyond the threshold for its type is escalated.

COD remittance: expected = sum of collected COD amounts on the run's POD records; remitted = amount the cashier records; equal → Reconciled, otherwise Discrepancy; a Reconciled or Resolved remittance cannot be edited.

A buyer may change the delivery address or instructions only while no shipment of the order is dispatched, no carrier booking is Booked or LabelIssued, and the client change window is open; the new address must pass BR-LOG-020; if the recalculated fee differs, the change is refused (Proposed).

Holding charge: free days start at Shipment.ReadyForPickupDateUtc; after them a daily charge accrues until collection, return or waiver; free days and daily charge are settings per client or outlet (values not stated); waivers need a reason.

LOG-018 KPIs are computed from the active RPT-002 KPI catalogue definitions (BR-RPT-010), so LOG-018 and RPT-010 show the same figures. Definitions proposed by LOG for the catalogue: on-time rate = shipments delivered on or before the promised latest date ÷ shipments delivered in the period; delivery success rate = shipments delivered or collected ÷ shipments that ended delivered, collected, returned to sender or lost in the period; average transit time = mean of DeliveryDateUtc − ShippedDateUtc.
Logistics tasks and seller pickups follow SM-LOG-04 and SM-LOG-10; a task is completed only by its matching scan or confirmation.
Address coordinates are stored in a plugin table keyed by AddressId with source (pin, provider, manual) and validation result; the native Address table is not changed.
An international postal shipment cannot be dispatched while its customs declaration is not Accepted, where CDS is integrated (Proposed).

Operational stages for ADM-007 (Proposed; stage definitions not stated, MG-06): awaiting pickup = a SellerPickup Scheduled or Missed, or a FulfilmentTask of a merchant-fulfilled line Allocated and not handed over; awaiting sorting = a LogisticsTask of type sort Created or Scheduled, or the last TRK-002 event ARRIVED_HUB; awaiting dispatch = a FulfilmentTask Packed or Staged, or a native shipment with no ShippedDateUtc; out for last-mile delivery = a RouteListItem OutForDelivery or the last TRK-002 event OUT_FOR_DELIVERY and no DeliveryDateUtc. A shipment with ReadyForPickupDateUtc or DeliveryDateUtc set is in none of these stages. The first matching stage in this order applies. The stage per order is ORD BR-ORD-015; ADM-007 shows both (AC-ADM-007-02-01).

Every LOG setting key is listed in the LOG plugin key catalogue (key, type, layer, secret flag, default); every carrier, geocoding, postal and printer credential is flagged secret, so packs refuse it and exports omit it (BR-PLT-013). LOG pages, widgets and scheduled tasks check the feature state through IC-PLT-02 (productfeature.<prd-id>, per store) before they show or run. LOG sends no message itself: its notifications are sent by TRK-005 through IC-TRK-04 SendEvent with event codes LOG registers at installation through IC-TRK-04 RegisterEventCode (Proposed names: Log.SellerPickupScheduled, Log.DropOffAccepted, Log.ExceptionEscalated, Log.CodDiscrepancy, Log.StaffAlert); shipment messages to buyers are TRK-012 templates; TRK-006 opt-outs apply (decision MSG-ROUTE).

Workflow steps (ADM-002) and other modules act on fulfilment only through the LOG fulfilment service (IC-LOG-07), which applies the LOG state models and BR-LOG-001; they never change order, shipment or task state directly. Workflow starts are queued requests raised from native events; consumers only enqueue.
basis: see ADM-002 (REQ-KTDA-WF-005); FIT (EventPublisher swallows consumer exceptions)

rule: Native admin shipment actions are intercepted by a global IAsyncActionFilter registered by the LOG plugin on Admin OrderController: SetAsDelivered and SetAsDeliveredSelected (BR-LOG-080), EditShippedDate, EditDeliveryDate and EditReadyForPickupDate (reason, correction event, audit — the native actions change the date without raising an event), SetTrackingNumber and AddShipment [POST] (S10 validation), DeleteShipment (refused while a carrier booking is active) and AddressEdit [POST] (refused while a carrier booking is active). A ModelReceivedEvent veto is not used: these actions do not check ModelState before saving. The filter is listed in the ADM extension register (BR-ADM-005); AddShipment [POST] also carries the ORD-010 shipment-guard host filter and the INV filter, each with its own check.

Native discount evaluation is used unchanged: active flag, dates, coupon code, limitation, requirement groups, maximum amount and quantity, and the native preferred-discount choice when discounts are not cumulative. The only change is the buy-X-get-Y subtotal (BR-MKT-003). MKT registers no IPriceCalculationService or IOrderTotalCalculationService override (owner CAT-042, decision OVR-REG); native discounts come last in the price precedence of BR-CAT-020.

Every redemption of a promo code or gift card is recorded natively (DiscountUsageHistory, GiftCardUsageHistory); every change to a discount or gift card is in the activity log and the platform audit trail.

Buy-X-get-Y: for a qualifying line, free units = floor(quantity / (X + Y)) × Y, priced at zero. MKT implements it as a provider called by the single IShoppingCartService override owned by CHK-003 (decision OVR-REG), inside GetSubTotalAsync, the single path used by cart display, order totals and order placement; MKT registers no override of its own. The native GetShoppingCartItemUnitPriceEvent is not used, because consumer exceptions are swallowed and it sets a unit price only.
basis: REQ-KTDA-MKT-002; FIT (ShoppingCartService.GetSubTotalAsync callers; EventPublisher); OVR-REG; Proposed (formula)

rule: Spend bands are separate non-cumulative order-subtotal discounts, each with a band requirement rule [lower, upper); at most one band applies.
A bundle discount applies only while every product of its set is in the cart; it is assigned to the set's products.
A pop-up is shown only if every rule matches (page, role, store, language, schedule, frequency); newsletter capture uses the native subscription with activation email.

When approval is enabled for a content type, a change by a user without Marketing.Core.Content.Approve becomes a revision and takes effect only when another user approves it; approval is enforced by an MKT action filter on the admin create and edit POST actions of the type (TopicController Create / Edit, BlogController BlogPostCreate / BlogPostEdit, and — only where the bundled Misc.News plugin is installed — the plugin controller NewsAdminController NewsItemCreate / NewsItemEdit, which replaced the core admin NewsController in 5.00).
basis: REQ-MPC-FR-313; FIT (these POST actions take TopicModel, BlogPostModel and the plugin NewsItemModel; 5.00.1: Plugins/Nop.Plugin.Misc.News/Admin/Controllers/NewsAdminController.cs:177, 226, [CheckPermission(News.Manage)]); Proposed

rule: Policy versions are immutable; every approved change to a policy topic creates a new version with an effective date; acceptance records refer to a version number.
Segment roles are maintained only by the segment task from the segment rule; manual changes to their membership are overwritten at the next run.
A referral reward is given once per referred customer, after the first order is Complete, and never when the referred customer matches the referrer by email, phone or device identifier.

A vendor discount always has VendorId = the current vendor and type "Assigned to SKUs", and can be mapped only to that vendor's products. Since nopCommerce 5.00 this is enforced natively by Admin DiscountController Create, Edit and ProductAddPopup [POST] for vendor users; MKT builds no action filter for it (VER-500) and removes its entry from the ADM extension register (BR-ADM-006).

Marketing tags, contact synchronisation and abandoned-cart reminders respect the consent rules of the country data-protection profile. Every analytics or marketing widget plugin (Widgets.GoogleAnalytics, Widgets.FacebookPixel, Misc.Omnisend, the MKT pop-up widget) is mapped to a cookie category in the SEC-007 widget-category map before go-live; unmapped non-necessary widgets are not allowed. Consent gating of widgets is done by the SEC-007 IWidgetPluginManager override (BR-SEC-020), not by MKT. A tag that needs consent is never put in SeoSettings.CustomHeadTags, which is not gated.

The Omnisend configuration page requires Configuration.ManagePlugins. Since nopCommerce 5.00 the bundled OmnisendAdminController enforces it natively on every Configure action, so MKT builds no action filter for it (VER-500) and removes its entry from the ADM extension register (BR-ADM-006). Misc.Brevo is not installed (decision OVR-REG; BR-TRK-021).

"N times only" limits are checked natively against usage history in the cart; because the placement lock that the CHK-003 IOrderProcessingService override reproduces once per checkout is per customer, the limit is also guarded at placement by the MKT-001 participant (IC-MKT-04 through IC-CHK-06): Reserve counts recorded uses plus open reservations under ILocker key 'mkt-discount-{DiscountId}' and refuses when the limit would be exceeded; Confirm ends the reservation once the native placement has written the usage row; Release or expiry ends it without a use. It is a placement participant, not a validator.
basis: FIT (DiscountService limitation check; OrderProcessingService named mutex per customer; OrderProcessingService inserts DiscountUsageHistory); Proposed (BR-CHK-020)

rule: MKT plugins (Platform core part and Engagement and loyalty pack): (a) check feature state through IC-PLT-02 IsEnabled (setting productfeature.<prd-id>, store then shared) before showing a page or widget or running a scheduled task for a store; (b) list every new setting key in the plugin key catalogue with key, type, layer, secret flag and default; (c) flag as secret the credentials of the bundled plugins MKT configures: GoogleAnalyticsSettings.ApiSecret and OmnisendSettings.ApiKey; the Facebook Pixel AccessToken is held in the plugin table FacebookPixelConfiguration, not in settings, and is never put in a configuration pack; (d) list every MKT action filter (since 5.00: the content-approval filter of BR-MKT-007 only) and provider registration (IC-MKT-01 as IC-CHK-05, IC-MKT-04 as IC-CHK-06) in the ADM extension register (BR-ADM-001); (e) register the MKT event codes (names Proposed, listed in BR-TRK-023: Mkt.Core.ContentRevisionPending, Mkt.Core.ContentRevisionDecided, Mkt.Core.ReferralRewarded) through IC-TRK-04 RegisterEventCode at installation and send them only through IC-TRK-04 SendEvent; TRK-006 preferences and opt-outs apply (MSG-ROUTE).

Order stages are a plugin entity. Each stage declares the native OrderStatus values (Pending, Processing, Complete, Cancelled) it may coexist with; the OrderStatus enum is never changed and OrderStatusId is never set directly by ORD.

A manual stage change may only use declared transitions. If the target stage needs a different native status, ORD calls the native service (CancelOrderAsync for Cancelled); Processing and Complete are reached only through native payment and shipping actions, so ORD refuses manual changes that would need them.

Stage auto-advance runs in consumers of native events (OrderPaidEvent, ShipmentSentEvent, ShipmentReadyForPickupEvent, ShipmentDeliveredEvent, OrderStatusChangedEvent, OrderRefundedEvent) and of the RET event Return.Completed (BR-RET-064). Consumers swallow exceptions, so a failed or undeclared auto-advance is written to a stage exceptions list that a scheduled task re-checks; no blocking logic is placed in consumers.

Order acceptance: OrderAcceptedEvent (new, published by the ORD service through IEventPublisher) carries OrderId, AcceptedOnUtc, AcceptedBy (buyer, staff or system) and Deemed (true when recorded by the acceptance-window task). It is published once per order, only from the delivery-mapped stage and only when no dispute is open (checked through IC-RET-01 HasOpenCase inside the order lock). PAY-007 consumes it to enqueue the escrow release; the release runs in PAY.
basis: Proposed; (PAY-007); product decision on order acceptance (2026-11-19)

rule: Line stage sets: ORD-002 holds the stage-set definitions and transitions per product type in the same configuration as order stages (default for service lines: SM-SVC-01 of SVC-005) and answers transition checks (IC-ORD-10). One owner per behaviour: the per-line state, its history and its change event belong to the module of the line type (SVC-005 ServiceOrderStage and Service.StageChanged); ORD keeps no per-line store. The order stage and the native OrderStatus are not derived from line stages unless an auto-advance rule says so.

Operational stage for ADM-007: taken from the operational code of the current order stage; if that stage has none and LOG-011 is enabled for the store, the stage of the order's first open shipment returned by LOG (IC-LOG-07 GetOperationalStage, BR-LOG-170), so the order row and its shipment rows agree; otherwise AwaitingPickup when no shipment exists, AwaitingDispatch when a shipment exists and is not shipped, OutForLastMileDelivery when Shipment.ShippedDateUtc is set and DeliveryDateUtc is empty. AwaitingSorting is set only from a stage fed by LOG or TRK-002 events. The client mapping is configuration.

Native admin order-edit actions (ChangeOrderStatus, CancelOrder, EditOrderTotals, EditOrderItem, DeleteOrderItem, EditShippingMethod, AddressEdit, AddProductToOrderDetails, OrderNoteDelete, Delete) are intercepted by a global IAsyncActionFilter registered by the ORD plugin; they need a reason code, and ChangeOrderStatus also needs Orders.Core.Status.Override. A ModelReceivedEvent veto is not used: most of these actions take an id or a form, and ChangeOrderStatus does not check ModelState. Payment actions are excluded: PAY intercepts them (BR-PAY-082).

Order-changing actions of ORD (stage change, cancellation, hold, partial supply, seller steps) run under ILocker key 'pay-order-{OrderId}', shared with PAY and INV-004; the action re-reads the order inside the lock and fails if its expected state no longer holds.

Buyer cancellation uses an ORD endpoint (native AllowCustomersCancelOrders stays off because the native action takes no reason and applies no policy). Cancellation is allowed only before fulfilment starts (no shipment; task not Packed or HandedOver) and within the policy window; it calls CancelOrderAsync(order, notifyCustomer: true). ORD raises no refund: RET-005 is the single owner of refund triggers and raises the Cancellation trigger for a paid order from OrderStatusChangedEvent; PAY-016 moves the money.
basis: REQ-MPC-FR-154; FIT (Nop.Web OrderController.CancelOrder; CanCancelOrder checks only != Cancelled); RET-005 single refund-trigger owner

rule: Seller rejection and deadline cancellation require a reason code; a configured penalty creates a SellerPenalty record that ORD passes to SEL through IC-SEL-05 (AddSellerCharge, source type Penalty, source reference = SellerPenalty ID, idempotent) when the penalty is created; this push is the only path, SEL does not read SellerPenalty at batch close; SEL-017 deducts it in settlement (payouts are SEL-017, commission rules SEL-016).

Seller task steps: New → Accepted → Packed → HandedOver. The task is created in state New by the ORD placement participant (IC-CHK-06 Confirm) for each sub-order. Hand over needs a shipment; for own-carrier sellers it calls ShipAsync, for postal-network fulfilment it starts LOG-011 pickup or LOG-022 drop-off and TRK-002 events change the shipment. The seller acts only on own sub-orders (ownership check in the ORD endpoint).

Partial supply never edits a paid order without the buyer's acceptance; on acceptance quantities are reduced by the ORD service (UpdateOrderTotalsAsync with UpdateOrderParameters, or IOrderService.UpdateOrderItemAsync when automatic total update is off), never through the native admin EditOrderItem action, so stock is not returned for unavailable quantities (no AdjustInventoryAsync call); money is returned only through a RET-005 refund trigger (IC-RET-04, source type PartialSupply), which PAY-016 executes.

Order numbers: native mask tokens {ID}, {YYYY}, {YY}, {MM}, {DD} plus the padded token {ID:n} through an ICustomNumberFormatter override (DI, INopStartup Order >= 3000); masks per store and optionally per order type.

ORD-009 does not override IPdfService: under decision OVR-REG DOC-001 owns that override (BR-DOC-001). ORD-009 supplies the Invoice and ConsolidatedReceipt document types and their template content, the invoice number, the issue rules and the ORD token provider (IC-ORD-07 through IC-DOC-02), which also serves proforma, contract, letter and Incoterm fields; PAY-025 prints fiscal number and QR through its own DOC token provider. Invoice issue jobs are enqueued by consumers and executed by a scheduled task; rendering is a DOC-001 call (IC-DOC-01).

An active hold blocks shipment creation and the shipment status actions. The hold check is an IC-ORD-11 shipment guard of the ORD-010 shipment-guard host (BR-ORD-055; the PAY-006 LC check and EGV-004 are the other providers), and an order-action guard with the CHK-003 IOrderProcessingService override for ShipAsync, ReadyForPickupAsync and DeliverAsync (IC-CHK-07). It does not block cancellation or payment.

Shipment-guard host (core, decision OVR-REG; D-01): ORD-010 owns the only IShipmentService.InsertShipmentAsync override (DI, INopStartup Order >= 3000). It calls every registered shipment guard provider (IC-ORD-11) in registration order and refuses the insert on the first refusal; a provider error refuses the insert (fail closed). An ORD action filter on Admin OrderController.AddShipment [POST] calls the same providers and shows the first refusal message before the native action runs (AddShipment does not check ModelState, so a ModelReceivedEvent veto is not used; an event consumer cannot block). Providers: ORD-010 hold, PAY-006 letter of credit (BR-PAY-030), EGV-004 application Issued (BR-EGV-008). Lot and serial capture is not a guard (IC-INV-07, BR-INV-070). Listed in the ADM extension register (BR-ADM-001).
basis: FIT (IShipmentService.InsertShipmentAsync; Admin OrderController.AddShipment); OVR-REG; D-01; Proposed (host in ORD-010)

rule: Service-level due time = start event time (moved to the next working day after the cut-off) + handling time of the level; cut-offs use the store time zone.

RFQ extends the bundled Misc.RFQ plugin without changing it: RfqService is a concrete class with non-virtual methods, so ORD adds side tables (RfqInvitation, RfqCustomLine, QuoteVendor, QuoteTerms, NegotiationRound, RfqQuestion) and its own services and controllers, and reuses native RequestQuote, Quote, QuoteItem, the price event and CreateShoppingCartAsync. ORD is the only module that writes Misc.RFQ tables; CAT-013 and SVC-001 start requests from a product page through IC-ORD-08, which inserts the RequestQuote through IRepository<RequestQuote> (RfqService has no public insert without the cart).
basis: FIT (Misc.RFQ PluginNopStartup registers RfqService as itself)

rule: A seller sees only the requests it is invited to and its own quotes; buyer answers to clarification questions are shared with all invited sellers.
Accepting one quote declines the other quotes of the same request; expired quotes cannot be accepted (native lazy expiry plus ORD expiry task).
Offer responses are converted into RFQ requests; there is no ranking, bidding or auction (D-02).
Requisition workflows run on the ADM-002 engine and ADM-006 queues; ORD stores the requisition and its form data only.
Contracts are versioned; only Approved versions can be issued or sent for signing; a Signed version is never edited, only amended.
A contract is Signed only when every party's signer quorum is met; signature evidence is stored as returned by the provider.
Call-off and drawdown orders never exceed the remaining contract quantity; each order links to its contract line.
The recurring task processes each cycle at most once (RecurringPaymentHistory check under ILocker key 'ord-recurring-{RecurringPaymentId}') and only for RecurringPaymentType.Manual methods.
A payment method is shown only if it is active, allowed for the store and customer role, and every routing rule that applies to it allows it.

Routing rule dimensions: store, country, customer role or type, location type (rural/urban, read from the LOG-004 coverage area ServiceArea.LocationType; PAY stores none), fulfilment (pickup/delivery), service type, order value range, seller, item.

Transaction statuses and transitions are those of state model SM-PAY-01. Native order PaymentStatus mapping: Initiated, Pending, AwaitingConfirmation, Failed → Pending (order stays retryable); Authorized → Authorized (MarkAsAuthorizedAsync); Successful → Paid (MarkOrderAsPaidAsync); Voided (only from Authorized) → Voided (VoidAsync / VoidOfflineAsync); Reversed or Refunded from Paid → Refunded or PartiallyRefunded (RefundAsync / RefundOfflineAsync if nothing was refunded before, otherwise PartiallyRefundAsync / PartiallyRefundOfflineAsync). The native order PaymentStatus is changed only through IOrderProcessingService, never by setting Order.PaymentStatusId directly.
Card data (number, expiry, security code) is never received, stored or logged by the platform; only gateway tokens and references.

Every provider call that can charge or refund carries an idempotency key (default Order.OrderGuid + AttemptNo); every callback is de-duplicated by provider reference and transaction status before MarkOrderAsPaidAsync is called — native CanMarkOrderAsPaid alone is not sufficient because it returns true for PartiallyRefunded orders.

Stock is decremented at order placement (native). The unpaid-order timeout, reminders and release are owned by PRD-INV-004: when the payment window for the payment method of the order expires, INV-004 applies its configured action (remind, flag or cancel); if the action is cancel, it cancels the order through IOrderProcessingService.CancelOrderAsync, which returns the stock. PAY keeps no separate stock hold and no timeout of its own. INV-004 cancels only if, under ILocker key 'pay-order-{OrderId}', the order PaymentStatus is still Pending and no PaymentTransaction for the order is Successful or Authorized; it calls CancelOrderAsync(order, notifyCustomer: true). CancelOrderAsync does not void or refund payments.

Group payment (Proposed): when CHK-004 places several sub-orders under one CheckoutSession, it processes payment once before any sub-order is saved (BR-CHK-006); PAY creates one PaymentTransaction for the checkout (merchant reference = CheckoutSession reference) with one share per seller, and links each sub-order through PaymentTransactionOrder when the CHK-003 placement host calls the PAY placement participant Confirm (IC-CHK-06) after saving it; the provider is charged once. A Paid result is applied by native placement to every sub-order; PAY never marks a sub-order paid twice. On success MarkOrderAsPaidAsync is called once per sub-order under 'pay-checkout-{CheckoutSessionId}' then 'pay-order-{OrderId}'; on failure all sub-orders stay Pending and retry is per checkout. Redirection adapters redirect for the checkout total from PostProcessPaymentAsync of the one order native checkout passes. A method whose adapter does not declare group support is not offered for a checkout with more than one sub-order. Until approved, CHK-004 is single-seller only.
basis: Proposed; OVR-REG; FIT (ProcessPaymentRequest.CustomValues; PostProcessPaymentRequest.Order; CheckoutController calls PostProcessPaymentAsync once)

rule: Payment references are unique per order and payment attempt, not guessable, and include a check digit (format Proposed).
A bank payment is matched only when reference and amount match; anything else is an exception.
COD is available only if every item and every seller in the cart allow it and the delivery address is in an allowed area.

No shipment may be created for an LC-paid order until the LC is Verified. PAY-006 enforces this only as a shipment guard provider (IC-ORD-11) to the single IShipmentService.InsertShipmentAsync override hosted by the core feature ORD-010 (BR-ORD-055, decision OVR-REG; core behaviour is not hosted in the B2B trade pack, D-01); PAY registers no shipment override and no AddShipment filter of its own. A ModelReceivedEvent veto is not used (AddShipment does not check ModelState); an event consumer cannot block.

Escrow releases follow the stages defined for the order; no release while a dispute is open, checked by calling RET HasOpenCase(orderId) (IC-RET-01) synchronously inside the ILocker key 'pay-order-{OrderId}' before each release; release jobs are enqueued by event consumers (ShipmentSentEvent, ShipmentDeliveredEvent, OrderAcceptedEvent) and executed by a scheduled task; the ADM-002 payment-release step calls the same release operation (IC-PAY-06) and the same checks apply.
Wallet balance never goes below zero; every change is a ledger entry with a reference.
Split = seller share + logistics fee + platform commission (+ tax on commission) = amount paid for the line, using the rule versions in force when the order was placed.
Partial refunds adjust fees, commission and split amounts in proportion to the refunded share of the line.
Amounts are rounded per line to the currency's minor unit; any rounding remainder goes to the platform commission line, so the parts always sum to the line amount.
A PaymentSplit carries a SettlementBatchId set only by SEL-017 inside its settlement lock; a split with a SettlementBatchId is never included in another batch.
Reconciliation classes: Matched, Unmatched — platform only, Unmatched — provider only, Timing difference.
Fee, commission and tax rules are versioned with an effective date; an order keeps the versions in force when placed.
Segregation of duties: the person who requests a refund above the threshold, or creates a disbursement batch, cannot approve it.

A refund cannot exceed Order.OrderTotal − Order.RefundedAmount (primary store currency), nor, per line, the line amount paid minus earlier line refunds. Order-level parts (BR-PAY-085) count against the order limit only.

Native admin payment actions (mark as paid, refund, refund offline, partial refund, void, void offline, capture) are intercepted by PAY through a global IAsyncActionFilter registered by the PAY plugin for Admin OrderController actions CaptureOrder, MarkOrderAsPaid, RefundOrder, RefundOrderOffline, VoidOrder, VoidOrderOffline and PartiallyRefundOrderPopup [POST] (a ModelReceivedEvent veto cannot be used: except the partial-refund popup these actions take no model); they are allowed only with Payments.Core.Transactions.CreateEditDelete (mark paid, void, capture) or Payments.Core.Refunds.Request plus approval (refunds), with a reason, and are audited. Native admin payment actions remain blocked for vendors.

Refund lifecycle: Initiated → Processing → Completed | Failed (SM-PAY-02). For asynchronous providers the native order refund is recorded only on Completed, through the offline refund methods; the native OrderRefunded notification is therefore sent once, on completion. Exception: for a transaction in SuccessfulAfterCancel the refund is provider-side only; on Completed PAY records it on the Refund record and an OrderNote and does not call native refund methods (the order PaymentStatus is Pending and they would throw); the order stays Cancelled; the shopper is notified by the PAY message template Pay.RefundAfterCancel.CustomerNotification (new, installed by the PAY plugin), not the native OrderRefunded template.

IC-PAY-05 order-level parts and orderless requests (Proposed). (1) A RET request may carry order-level parts (component Shipping, PaymentFee or CheckoutAttribute, amount) beside or instead of order lines; each part is stored as a RefundLine with its component and no OrderItemId; the total of lines and parts is checked against BR-PAY-081 and recorded through the native refund method for the order amount; split and fee adjustments (BR-PAY-051) apply to line amounts only. (2) A RET request with source type PlacementFailure carries no order ID but the CheckoutSession reference and the group PaymentTransaction ID; its amount cannot exceed the share of that transaction linked to no sub-order minus earlier refunds of it; the refund is provider-side only and no native order refund method is called (as for SuccessfulAfterCancel, BR-PAY-083).
basis: Proposed (RET IC-RET-04, AC-RET-005-05-03, AC-RET-005-05-04); FIT (OrderProcessingService.PartiallyRefundOfflineAsync checks OrderTotal − RefundedAmount)

rule: The PAY refund request operation (IC-PAY-05) is the only entry for refunds raised outside PAY and accepts calls only from RET-005 (refund-trigger owner); each request carries an idempotency key and a source reference; a repeated key returns the first Refund. PAY-internal refunds (finance staff, SuccessfulAfterCancel) use the same service.
basis: Proposed (product refund-trigger decision: RET-005 single owner); BR-RET-041

rule: Risk rules have a type (velocity, device, model score from AI-006, other), an action (Flag or Block; Flag may also request an ORD-010 hold), a threshold and an on/off state; Block is evaluated before payment as a CHK placement validator (IC-PAY-03); every firing raises Risk.Flagged; every change is audited and, as a PLT-004 controlled configuration type (IC-PLT-03), approved before it applies.
Every manual intervention on a payment needs a reason and is written to the audit trail.

Provider credentials are stored encrypted per client instance and never exported in configuration packs; every PAY setting key that holds a credential, key or token is flagged secret in the PAY key catalogue so the PLT pack loader refuses it and exports omit it.

Every PAY setting key is listed in the PAY key catalogue (key, type, layer, secret flag, default) so configuration-pack validation accepts it (NFR-X-008); PAY pages, widgets and scheduled tasks check the feature state through IC-PLT-02 (setting productfeature.<prd-id>, two-level) for the store before they run.
Where e-invoicing applies, an invoice is final only when the authority accepts it; credit notes reference the original invoice.

A receivable is created per on-account invoice, at invoice issue, with due date = issue date + CreditAccount.PaymentTermsDays (CHK-016); the debtor is a customer, a company or a vendor (SEL-025 commission invoices).

A receivable offered to a lender (FIN-002) is locked against a second offer; once Assigned, its payee is the lender, allocations received by the client for it are flagged for forwarding to the lender, and the PAY-010 splits of its invoice lines are never returned to SEL-017 as eligible for settlement. A payment the buyer makes to the lender is recorded by FIN through AllocateExternal with the lender reference.
A shift cash-up records expected and counted cash; a closed shift cannot be edited.
Orders paid by direct payment to the seller create no split, escrow or payout; refunds are made by the seller through PAY endpoints and recorded by the platform.

Unpaid-order reminder and cancellation configuration rule (VER-500): the native 5.00 pending-order reminders (ReminderSettings.PendingOrdersEnabled, install default on; message templates Reminders.PendingOrderFollowUp1 and 2, active by default after 3 and 10 days; email only) are sent for every order with PaymentStatus Pending, whatever the payment method, including on-account (CHK-016), letter-of-credit (PAY-006), escrow (PAY-007) and bank-transfer (PAY-005) orders that are pending by design. Every configuration pack sets PendingOrdersEnabled off unless the client asks for it; the payment-pending message is the PAY-011 notification (event code Pay.Status.Pending through TRK-005). The native automatic cancellation of unpaid orders (OrderSettings.AutoCancelEnabled, install default off; AutoCancelOrdersTask cancels through CancelOrderAsync after one AutoCancelDelay for all methods except AutoCancelIgnoredPaymentMethods) stays off while the unpaid-order timeout per payment method is INV-004 (decision INV-HOLD); if INV-004 adopts it, AutoCancelIgnoredPaymentMethods lists every on-account, letter-of-credit and escrow method.
basis: VER-500; FIT (ReminderSettings.cs:18; ProcessPendingOrdersTask.cs:54-90; AutoCancelOrdersTask.cs:56-75; InstallRequiredData.cs:1164-1180, 1895-1899, 2207); Proposed

rule: PAY sends no email or SMS itself. Native templates and the PAY template Pay.RefundAfterCancel.CustomerNotification go through IWorkflowMessageService (single override TRK-005); every other PAY notification in §13 goes through IC-TRK-04 SendEvent with a PAY event code registered at installation through IC-TRK-04 RegisterEventCode. Each event code has the name of the message key that holds its default text. TRK-006 opt-outs apply to all.
basis: Proposed; owner decision on messages (TRK-005 sends all notifications); see TRK-005 (BR-TRK-020)

rule: One nopCommerce installation and one database per client per environment (live, test). All instances of all clients run the same product release.
A client's live instance can be set Active only after its test instance is Active and a UAT sign-off (reference, signed by, date) is recorded.

Go-live checklist per live instance (Proposed): HTTPS on every store; proxy forwarded headers when TLS ends at a proxy; TLS versions and ciphers; encryption at rest for database, files and backups; WAF and DDoS protection; database login with insert and select only on audit tables; region per DP-01; distributed cache enabled with more than one web node; until PLT-027 idempotency keys (P2) are delivered, checkout is served by one web node only (the native placement lock is per host; CHK-008). A live instance is set Active only when every item is recorded as passed.
basis: Proposed (SEC hosting items, BR-SEC-070); FIT (Store.SslEnabled; HostingConfig; DistributedCacheConfig)

rule: Isolation checklist per instance: own database and connection string, own App_Data (appsettings.json, plugins.json, DataProtectionKeys), own media storage, own credentials; a shared Redis or SQL Server cache server is allowed only with a unique DistributedCacheConfig.InstanceName per instance; Store.SslEnabled true for every store; stores never separate two clients.

Pack layers merge in the order global, country, vertical, client, then store entries (Proposed: the country layer is the one the workbook Config pack schema marks "country", for example tax, fiscal adapter, payment routing defaults, carriers, law profile, retention and SMS rules). A higher layer overrides only the keys it states; store entries apply to the named store only. A pack set names exactly one country pack, versioned and checksummed like every other pack; how one instance serves several countries is Not stated in source.
basis: CFG-01 (order to be extended with the country layer); D; Proposed (country layer)

rule: Run-time resolution has two levels only: the Setting row of the store, else the row with StoreId 0, else the settings-class default (SettingService.LoadSettingAsync with loadSharedValueIfNotFound). The loader writes merged shared layers as StoreId 0 rows and store entries as StoreId n rows; when a store entry is removed from the pack, the store row is deleted. No run-time layer resolver is built.

Plugin enablement lives in files and settings and the loader writes both: the installed list is App_Data/plugins.json (installedPlugins.json and InstalledPlugins.txt are obsolete), changed only through IPluginService.PreparePluginToInstallAsync / PreparePluginToUninstallAsync and effective after an application restart; store and role limits are LimitedToStores / LimitedToCustomerRoles in each plugin's plugin.json, written through PluginDescriptor.Save on every web node; active-provider lists are settings (paymentsettings.activepaymentmethodsystemnames, shippingsettings.activeshippingratecomputationmethodsystemnames, shippingsettings.activepickuppointprovidersystemnames, taxsettings.activetaxprovidersystemname, widgetsettings.activewidgetsystemnames, catalogsettings.activesearchprovidersystemname). Deployment must not overwrite plugin.json limits; at application start the PLT plugin reconciles each node's plugin.json limits with the last applied state.
basis: FIT (NopPluginDefaults.PluginsInfoFilePath, InstalledPluginsFilePath; PluginsInfo.SaveAsync; PluginDescriptor.Save; AppStartedConsumer); L1 section 6.5; Proposed (reconcile)

rule: Secrets are never in packs, exports, promotions or clones: securitysettings.encryptionkey, captchasettings.recaptchaprivatekey, translationsettings.googleapikey, translationsettings.deeplauthkey, artificialintelligencesettings.geminiapikey, artificialintelligencesettings.chatgptapikey, artificialintelligencesettings.deepseekapikey, proxysettings.password, taxsettings.hmrcclientsecret, shippingsettings.googlemapsapikey, EmailAccount.Password and ClientSecret, appsettings.json; the credential keys of the bundled plugins: facebookexternalauthsettings.clientsecret, brevosettings.apikey, brevosettings.smtpkey, brevosettings.marketingautomationkey, omnisendsettings.apikey, googleanalyticssettings.apisecret, paypalcommercesettings.secretkey, zettlesettings.apikey, zettlesettings.webhookkey, avalarataxsettings.licensekey, upssettings.clientsecret, cloudflareimagessettings.accesstoken; and every product plugin setting flagged secret in the key catalogue. Secrets are entered per instance.
basis: CFG-01; FIT (SecuritySettings.EncryptionKey; CaptchaSettings.ReCaptchaPrivateKey; TranslationSettings; ArtificialIntelligenceSettings; ProxySettings.Password; TaxSettings.HmrcClientSecret; ShippingSettings.GoogleMapsApiKey; EmailAccount; FacebookExternalAuthSettings.ClientSecret; BrevoSettings; OmnisendSettings; GoogleAnalyticsSettings.ApiSecret; PayPalCommerceSettings.SecretKey; ZettleSettings; AvalaraTaxSettings.LicenseKey; UPSSettings.ClientSecret; CloudflareImagesSettings.AccessToken)

rule: Instance-bound items are never promoted or cloned: Store.Url, Store.Hosts, Store.SslEnabled, store company details, logos (clone only), e-mail accounts, secrets (BR-PLT-013), the instance profile.

A pack apply holds ILocker key 'plt-config-write'; database writes run in one TransactionScope; file writes follow and are compensated from the pre-apply snapshot on failure; the setting cache is cleared once at the end.
basis: Proposed; FIT (EntityRepository bulk writes use INopDataProvider.CreateTransactionScope with TransactionScopeOption.Required, BaseDataProvider.cs:503-533; ILocker)

rule: Each applied pack set is stamped (codes, versions, checksums, user, time). Applying an identical pack set changes nothing.

Transaction-type and single-transaction overrides apply only to ADM-004 parameters and ADM-011 templates, never to native Setting rows; a reason is mandatory; every override is recorded as a deviation.

Controlled keys: writes from admin requests are captured into a change set by the PLT action filter and the PLT ISettingService override (DI, INopStartup Order >= 3000, registered in the ADM-001 extension register); the change set is validated, previewed, approved (impact Low: one approver; High: two different approvers; never the requester) and applied through the base SettingService. In a Test instance a valid change set is applied at once. Writes outside admin requests (pack loader, plugin install, scheduled tasks) are not captured. The override implements the asynchronous members only; nopCommerce 5.00.1 has no synchronous ISettingService members.
basis: D; FC-M22-005; Proposed; FIT (SettingService public virtual write methods; Libraries/Nop.Services/Configuration/ISettingService.cs)

rule: A change set is applied only if the current value of each key still equals the old value recorded in it; otherwise it becomes Stale.
Every Setting write, controlled or not, is recorded with actor, time, key, store, old and new value by the SEC-004 IRepository<> decorator.
Rollback creates a new change set with earlier values; it follows BR-PLT-020 and BR-PLT-021.

Feature state is setting productfeature.<prd-id> (lower case) with the two-level resolution of BR-PLT-011 and default off; Platform core features are always on (D-01); a feature can be on only if every feature it depends on is on.
Every product plugin runs on the SQL Server, MySQL and PostgreSQL data providers: schema through FluentMigrator migrations, data access through the nopCommerce data layer, no provider-specific SQL.

Core modifications in this module are limited to PLT-018 (admin views) and PLT-027 (row version on core tables and the repository check), as registered in L1 section 6.3; each is a separate commit tagged with the PRD ID on the product fork.

Retention: one rule per record type (period, action Archive, Anonymise or Delete). Delete removes rows physically (repository predicate delete); Archive verifies the archive copy before removal; records under legal hold or linked to an open payment, refund, dispute or receivable are skipped.

Every record type that holds personal or business records is registered with the retention engine by its owning module (IC-PLT-08) with a hold check; the owning module names the type, PLT-020 runs the rule. Audit-trail retention works on closed segments only (SEC-004).
A release is deployed to a client's test instance and passes the regression set before its live instance; post-upgrade checks cover incompatible plugins, pack validity and the extension register.
A rate provider returns rates relative to CurrencySettings.PrimaryExchangeRateCurrencyId and leaves out any rate that moves more than the configured tolerance (default not stated).
Idempotency keys are scoped by customer and route; the first response is stored and replayed for the key retention period; a reused key with a different body is refused.
Optimistic concurrency: an update of a row-versioned table succeeds only if the row version read is unchanged; otherwise the user gets the current values and nothing is written.

Imported or machine-generated translations are Unchecked until a reviewer marks them Checked; a change of the source text resets the translation to Unchecked. PLT-025 is the only owner of translation status: AI-001 approval sets Checked through IC-PLT-09 and keeps no status of its own.

Messages raised inside a client instance (change sets pending, decided or stale; pack apply failed or awaiting decision; post-upgrade check failed; rate outside tolerance) are sent through TRK-005; PLT registers its event codes through IC-TRK-04 RegisterEventCode at installation (names Proposed): Platform.ChangeSetPending, Platform.ChangeSetDecided, Platform.PackApplyAttention, Platform.UpgradeCheckFailed, Platform.RateNotApplied. Messages about provisioning and instance status (PLT-001), monitoring (PLT-014) and backups (PLT-016) are sent by the provisioning pipeline or the monitoring platform outside the client instance; they go to the platform team and the client contact, never to customers.
A Suspended instance closes every store (StoreInformationSettings.StoreClosed true) and restores the previous values when re-activated; users with PublicStore.AccessClosedStore keep access.

Plugin build baseline for nopCommerce 5.00: every product plugin, and every third-party plugin or AFR extension in a release, targets net10.0, declares SupportedVersions "5.00", uses FluentMigrator 8.0.1 and only the asynchronous nopCommerce APIs (the synchronous IRepository, ISettingService, ILocalizationService, ILogger, IEventPublisher.Publish, IStoreContext and IStoreMappingService members were removed in 5.00). A plugin with no 5.00 build blocks the release of the features that depend on it.

The RET status of a return follows SM-RET-01. The native ReturnRequestStatus is changed only by RET services through IReturnRequestService.UpdateReturnRequestAsync, using the mapping in SM-RET-01. A status change posted from the native admin edit page (Admin ReturnRequestController.Edit [POST]) is checked by a RET action filter against SM-RET-01; a change not allowed is refused with message Ret.StatusChangeNotAllowed and nothing is saved. The same filter refuses changes to ReturnedQuantity on that page, because the native action adjusts stock directly (IProductService.AdjustInventoryAsync); restocking goes only through RET-004 and IC-INV-01.
basis: Proposed; FIT (the admin Edit POST takes ReturnRequestModel and checks ModelState; an action filter is used because event consumers swallow exceptions)

rule: For each return request RET stores the reason ID and action ID chosen; reports and rules use these IDs, not the localised names that the native record keeps.

An order item is eligible for return only if: native returns are enabled; the order is Complete; the product is not NotReturnable; the RET rule that applies (BR-RET-011) allows it; the rule window counted from its start has not passed; and quantity remains after earlier requests that are not Cancelled. Applied by a DI override of IReturnRequestService.GetReturnRequestAvailabilityAsync.

Rule precedence: native Product.NotReturnable, then product rule, then seller rule, then category rule, then the global setting. When RET rules set windows, ReturnRequestSettings.NumberOfDaysReturnRequestAvailable is 0 or not shorter than the longest rule window, because the native order-level check runs first.

Eligibility is enforced on submit by a RET action filter on ReturnRequestController.ReturnRequestSubmit [POST] and by a DI override of IReturnRequestService.InsertReturnRequestAsync; a ModelReceivedEvent veto is not used because the action does not check ModelState.

Each approved return records the shipping model applied (merchant-paid, customer-paid, shared, client-subsidised). Customer-paid and shared models create a return-delivery fee (RET-006); merchant-paid models are charged to the seller through IC-SEL-05 AddSellerCharge (source type ReturnShipping, idempotent on the return reference) and deducted by SEL-017 settlement; client-subsidised models create no charge in the shop.
On every change of the native return status RET sends the native ReturnRequestStatusChanged.CustomerNotification through IWorkflowMessageService, and the channels configured for the event in TRK-005.
basis: FC-M15-016 (buyer informed at each step); FIT (native sends it only on the admin Notify customer button)

rule: Refund amount requested for a return line = (OrderItem.PriceInclTax / OrderItem.Quantity) x accepted quantity, minus the fees of RET-006, never below zero. Treatment of shipping and order-level discounts: Not stated in source — requires confirmation.

Each refund trigger has a unique idempotency key "RET-{SourceType}-{SourceId}-{OrderItemId}"; for an order-level part the component name replaces the OrderItemId, and for PlacementFailure the OrderItemId is 0. A second trigger with the same key sends nothing to PAY.

Refund source-type register (RET-005 is the single owner of refund triggers; every automatic refund outside PAY starts here). Source type, raising module, how it is raised, and who computes the amount: Return (RET-004 inspection; RET, BR-RET-040); Cancellation (RET consumer of the native OrderStatusChangedEvent for a paid order cancelled by any path: ORD-004 buyer, seller or deadline cancellation, ORD-006 rejected proposal, INV-004, admin, CHK-004 staff resolution; RET, amount still refundable); ServiceFailure (RET consumer of SVC-005 Service.Failed; amount rule Not stated in source); Case (RET-007 accepted refund remedy; RET, decided remedy amount); BookingCancellation and ProviderNoShow (SVC-003, IC-RET-04; SVC, BR-SVC-021); DepositRefund (SVC-004, IC-RET-04; SVC); PolicyIssueFailed (FIN-003, IC-RET-04; FIN, BR-FIN-005); PartnerFulfilmentFailed (FIN-005, IC-RET-04; FIN, BR-FIN-005); ApplicationRejected (EGV-002, IC-RET-04; EGV); PartialSupply (ORD-006, IC-RET-04 through IC-ORD-05; ORD, BR-ORD-033); PlacementFailure (CHK-004 staff resolution of a PlacementException, IC-RET-04; CHK, share of the unsaved sub-order, BR-CHK-007). IC-RET-04 refuses a source type that is not in this register or that is raised by a module other than the one named. A new source type is added only by a change to this rule.
basis: Proposed (refund-trigger decision: RET-005 single owner; BR-SVC-021; BR-FIN-005; EGV-002; IC-ORD-05; SM-CHK-01)

rule: Return fees are versioned rules with an effective date; a return uses the rule versions in force on the date the return was requested; fees never make the refund negative.

A dispute case follows SM-RET-02. A case closes as Closed only after the customer accepts the remedy; otherwise it closes only as ClosedNoResponse (by staff, after the acceptance wait time), Withdrawn (by the customer) or ClosedExternal.
Every case step, decision, evidence addition and escalation is written to the case log with actor and time.

HasOpenCase(orderId) is true while any case of the order is not Closed, ClosedNoResponse, Withdrawn or ClosedExternal; PAY uses it before releasing escrow or confirming disputed payments; ORD-002 uses it before recording order acceptance.

Return.Completed is published once per return, after the inspection with outcome Accepted or PartiallyAccepted is committed; it carries OrderId, ReturnRequestIds, Outcome, AcceptedQuantity and CompletedOnUtc. It is a notification only: ORD maps it to the stage Returned; no consumer may change money or stock from it.
Only the parties of a case (customer, the linked seller) and staff with case permissions can read or post case messages; hidden messages are kept and are visible to staff.
Case timers come from SLA policies in the SLA component (CRM-014); a breach escalates the case one level of the escalation matrix and notifies the assignee and the next level.
A case file exported to an external body contains the summary, all evidence, the case log and the full message thread; the file hash and the export are recorded.
Return and dispute records are purged only through PLT-020 retention rules, never while a case is open or under legal hold.

Platform conformance (all RET features): every new RET setting key is listed in the RET plugin key catalogue (key, type, layer, secret flag, default) so pack validation accepts it; RET holds no credential of its own (carrier credentials are LOG settings), and any key added later that holds a credential, key or token is flagged secret. RET pages, widgets and scheduled tasks run for a store only when IC-PLT-02 IsEnabled(productfeature.<RET feature ID>) is true for that store. All RET writes go through IRepository<> so SEC-004 captures old and new values; business audit events AUD-RET-nnn are written through IC-SEC-01 WriteAsync with a correlation id.
basis: Proposed (BR-PLT-013, AC-PLT-003-01-04, AC-PLT-022-02-01; BR-SEC-010, BR-SEC-011, BR-SEC-014)

rule: Files (decision SINGLE-FILTER): RET evidence and case-message uploads are checked only by the ADM-008 upload policy, for the upload contexts "return evidence" and "case attachment" that the RET plugin registers with ADM-008 at installation; RET has no file-type or size check of its own except the number of files per return (setting). Downloads of RET files through Nop.Web DownloadController.GetFileUpload or Admin DownloadController.DownloadFile are decided by the single SEC-002 ownership filter (BR-SEC-005); RET is a rule provider to it and allows the shopper of the order, users of the vendor that owns the item, the parties of the case, and staff holding Orders.ReturnRequestsView or Returns.Core.Cases.View.
Sellers act on returns and cases only through RET seller endpoints that check the order item belongs to their vendor; the native return-request permissions are never granted to Vendors.
basis: FIT (no vendor filter in admin ReturnRequestController; DefaultPermissionConfigManager)

rule: Native reports are used as delivered; they are not modified. New in-platform panels are added through admin widget zones.

Every KPI shown in the BI platform comes from one active KPI catalogue definition (code, formula, unit); a definition change creates a new version with an effective date; the same definition is used by every dashboard (RPT-002, RPT-010, LOG-018).

Money amounts in reports and dashboards are labelled with their currency. Native order amounts are in the primary store currency; for orders with fixed per-currency prices (CAT-042) these vary with the rate at placement, so customer-currency totals are offered as well.

Reports and dashboards that group by financial period take their period boundaries from the PLT-012 fiscal-calendar service (FiscalCalendarSettings, client layer) when PLT-012 (P2) is delivered; until then calendar years, quarters and months are used and shown as such; calendar months are used only where the report says so.

Extract modes: ChangeFeed (from the SEC-004 change records) for tables without an update timestamp, Timestamp for tables with UpdatedOnUtc, IdRange for insert-only tables, Full when none applies. Event consumers are not used to capture changes, because some writes publish no event and consumers swallow exceptions.
basis: FIT (no UpdatedOnUtc on Order, OrderItem, Customer, Shipment; L1 §6.3 SEC-004 note); Proposed

rule: Fields marked for pseudonymisation or removal are treated before the data leaves nopCommerce; the hashing key stays in the client instance and is never exported.

External consumers (BI tools, warehouse readers, other systems) get read-only access to defined views or delivered files only; never write access to the shop database; credentials are stored encrypted per client instance.
The public page shows only aggregates from a snapshot; groups below the minimum group size are suppressed; no field classed as personal data is used.

Platform conformance (all RPT features): every new RPT setting key is listed in the RPT plugin key catalogue (key, type, layer, secret flag, default); keys that hold a credential, key or token (BI and external-consumer credentials, the pseudonymisation hashing key) are flagged secret, so the pack loader refuses them and exports omit them. RPT pages, widgets and scheduled tasks (extracts, snapshots, deliveries) run for a store only when IC-PLT-02 IsEnabled(productfeature.<RPT feature ID>) is true for that store. RPT writes its own tables through IRepository<>; business audit events AUD-RPT-nnn are written through IC-SEC-01 WriteAsync with a correlation id.
basis: Proposed (BR-PLT-013, AC-PLT-003-01-04, AC-PLT-022-02-01; BR-SEC-010, BR-SEC-011, BR-SEC-014); CFG-01

rule: Imported spend for a source and date range replaces any earlier import for the same scope.

All traffic is HTTPS: Store.SslEnabled is true for every store; behind a proxy HostingConfig.UseProxy and the forwarded headers are set; adapters use HTTPS endpoints only; packs cannot set DefaultPasswordFormat to Clear or Encrypted.

Secrets are per client instance and never in configuration packs: SecuritySettings.EncryptionKey, captcha private key, adapter credentials, export signing key. Every new SEC setting key is listed in the SEC plugin key catalogue with key, type, layer, secret flag and default (NFR-X-008); the signing key and the security-monitoring export credentials are flagged secret, so packs refuse them and exports omit them (BR-PLT-013).

No card data: since nopCommerce 5.00 the platform stores no card data (ProcessPaymentResult.AllowStoringCreditCardNumber, admin EditCreditCardInfo and the bundled Payments.Manual were removed; the Order card fields are obsolete and unused); product payment plugins add no card storage of their own; card adapters use a hosted page or gateway-hosted fields.
The application accepts public traffic only through the edge service; client IP addresses are taken from the forwarded header of known proxies only.

Uploaded-file access (Proposed; owner decision Download ownership): a SEC action filter on Nop.Web ShoppingCartController.UploadFileProductAttribute, UploadFileCheckoutAttribute and ReturnRequestController.UploadFileReturnRequest [POST] records UploadOwnership (download GUID, uploading customer, product). ONE SEC ownership filter covers Nop.Web DownloadController.GetFileUpload and Admin DownloadController.DownloadFile. It first calls every registered download-access rule provider (IC-SEC-05). If one or more providers claim the file, the file is served only when every claiming provider returns Allow. If no provider claims it, the base rule applies: GetFileUpload serves a file only to its uploader, to non-vendor users holding Orders.OrdersView, or to vendor users for files of their own products; DownloadFile serves vendor users only files of their own products. Every refusal shows Sec.FileAccessDenied and writes AUD-SEC-012. No other module registers a filter on these two actions. File type and size checks are ADM-008 (BR-ADM-060); SEC adds none.
basis: Proposed; FIT (DownloadController.GetFileUpload and Admin DownloadController.DownloadFile have no ownership check)

rule: Audit capture: a decorator of IRepository<> registered by the SEC plugin INopStartup (Order greater than 10) records every insert, update and delete of audited entities through every repository method, with old values from LoadOriginalCopyAsync and new values; entity events (EntityUpdatedEvent etc.) are not used for capture, because they carry only the new entity and are not raised for publishEvent false or predicate deletes. Only the SEC plugin decorates IRepository<>. Since nopCommerce 5.00 the interface has only async members, so the decorator implements InsertAsync, UpdateAsync, DeleteAsync (entity, list and predicate) and passes the read members through.
basis: FIT (5.00.1: Libraries/Nop.Data/IRepository.cs; NopDbStartup Order 10, Libraries/Nop.Data/NopDbStartup.cs:88; L1 §6.3 PRD-SEC-004; NFR-X-003)

rule: Writes that bypass the repository are covered by SEC overrides: AclService.SaveAclAsync and StoreMappingService.SaveStoreMappingsAsync (direct INopDataProvider.UpdateEntityAsync). Other direct data-provider writes exist only in installation code.

Redaction and ignore lists: values of redacted fields (CustomerPassword.Password and PasswordSalt, Setting values of keys flagged secret in BR-PLT-013 or in a plugin key catalogue, code and token hashes) are never written to the audit trail; the change itself is recorded with the field or key name; updates that change only ignored fields (for example last-activity times) are not audited. Both lists are configuration.

Integrity: audit events are append-only; the chain writer assigns sequence numbers and hashes (hash of canonical content plus previous hash) under ILocker key 'sec-audit-chain'; verification recomputes the chain; exports and integrity statements carry signed manifests. No product function updates or deletes an audit event; the application database login has insert and select rights only on audit tables (hosting).

Business events: modules write their AUD-<AREA>-nnn events through IC-SEC-01 (IAuditTrail.WriteAsync) with a correlation id per request; the native activity log is not an audit substitute, because it can be deleted (Customers.ActivityLogDelete) and holds no old values.
The entity change and its audit insert run in one database transaction; if the audit insert fails the change is rolled back and an error is logged (fail closed).
Audit events are kept for the configured retention period (default not stated); after it, whole closed segments are archived or removed with a signed checkpoint that keeps the chain verifiable.
Security exports (to monitoring or incident tools) are produced by scheduled tasks from the audit store in sequence order; event consumers are not used to export.

Before a visitor makes a cookie choice only necessary cookies are set; widget plugins mapped to a non-accepted category are not loaded (SEC override of IWidgetPluginManager.LoadActivePluginsAsync); each choice is logged with banner version.

Server-side analytics events are not gated by the cookie banner: when the country profile says they need consent, or the value is not configured, GoogleAnalyticsSettings.EnableEcommerce stays false (pack validation and a SEC action filter on WidgetsGoogleAnalyticsController.Configure [POST], listed in BR-ADM-006). Since nopCommerce 5.00 the plugin also sends add-to-cart, remove-from-cart and wishlist events on every cart change without an EnableEcommerce check, gated only by IWidgetPluginManager.IsPluginActiveAsync(Widgets.GoogleAnalytics), which does not go through LoadActivePluginsAsync; the SEC-007 override of IWidgetPluginManager therefore also answers IsPluginActiveAsync for a widget mapped to a cookie category with the consent of the current visitor (false without consent) (VER-500). Other plugins that send personal data from event consumers are listed in the processing register (SEC-012) with the same consent decision.
Breach deadlines and notice rules come only from the country profile; no legal value is coded; a missing value is shown as not configured and alerted.

One data-protection profile per country (shared with CHK-009 for the e-transactions part); law names are text; every legal value is configuration; the go-live checklist fails while a required value or a required transfer record is missing.

Auditor access is read-only and time-boxed: Auditor role with native *View permissions and Security.Core.AuditTrail.View; start and end are checked on every request through the single IAM override of IPermissionService; searches are limited to the engagement period and stores.
basis: D; FC-M20-005; FIT (native permission split, unchanged in 5.00.1); BR-IAM-060

rule: Masking is applied by a SEC global result filter on admin view models and JSON results, and by the SEC override of IExportManager for staff exports; on any masking error the value is hidden (fail closed); reveals are logged.
basis: D; FIT (PublishModelEventsAttribute raises ModelPreparedEvent to consumers that swallow errors)

rule: Extension register: every DI override and global action filter of the product is listed in the ADM extension register (BR-ADM-001), which is the single register (decision OVR-REG); SEC does not keep a copy.
