SEC-owned entries: the IRepository<> decorator (SEC-004), overrides of AclService.SaveAclAsync and StoreMappingService.SaveStoreMappingsAsync (SEC-004), IWidgetPluginManager.LoadActivePluginsAsync (SEC-007, owner under OVR-REG), IExportManager and the masking result filter (SEC-014), the upload-ownership recording filter and the single download-ownership filter on GetFileUpload and Admin DownloadFile with its IC-SEC-05 rule providers (BR-SEC-005). SEC checks at each release that every interface has one overriding plugin (owners per OVR-REG) and that every register entry is in the penetration-test scope (BR-SEC-081).
No Increment with a new high or critical vulnerability in the dependency scan is released (Definition of Done criterion 5).

Known platform findings re-checked in nopCommerce 5.00.1, each in the penetration-test scope with its product control: (1) resolved natively in 5.00 — the Misc.Brevo and Misc.Omnisend configuration actions now require Configuration.ManagePlugins (Brevo is still not installed under OVR-REG; its GetSynchronizationInfo action checks only AuthorizeAdmin and returns a synchronisation status text); (2) resolved natively in 5.00 — Admin DiscountController.ProductAddPopup [POST] refuses another vendor's discount and skips other vendors' products, so the MKT vendor discount filter is withdrawn (BR-MKT-011); (5) new in 5.00 — the HTML-editor file manager elFinder (ElFinderController.Connector, permission System.HtmlEditor.ManagePictures) writes files through its own library with its own allow-list (control: ADM-008 upload filter on Connector, BR-ADM-060); (3) Admin ArtificialIntelligenceController.GenerateMetaTags has no CheckPermission (control: AI action filter, BR-AI-004); (4) DownloadController.GetFileUpload and Admin DownloadController.DownloadFile serve files by GUID without ownership check, and upload file types are checked only in the browser (controls: the single SEC download-ownership filter with its IC-SEC-05 rule providers, BR-SEC-005; ADM-008 upload policy, BR-ADM-060).
basis: FIT (5.00.1: Plugins/Nop.Plugin.Misc.Brevo/Controllers/BrevoController.cs:227-562; Plugins/Nop.Plugin.Misc.Omnisend/Controllers/OmnisendAdminController.cs:73-137; Presentation/Nop.Web/Areas/Admin/Controllers/DiscountController.cs:487-512; ArtificialIntelligenceController.cs:53 (no CheckPermission); Presentation/Nop.Web/Controllers/DownloadController.cs:168; Admin DownloadController.cs:39; ElFinderController.cs:42-43); owner decision Download ownership; VER-500

rule: Messages: every SEC notification (breach notices to affected people, chain-broken, export-backlog, breach-deadline, auditor-access, impact-assessment review and profile-incomplete alerts) is sent by TRK-005 (owner decision Messages outside TRK). SEC registers its event codes at installation through IC-TRK-04 RegisterEventCode (names Proposed, listed in BR-TRK-023: Sec.BreachNotice, Sec.Core.AuditChainBroken, Sec.Core.ExportBacklog, Sec.Core.BreachDeadline, Sec.Core.AuditorAccess, Sec.Core.ImpactAssessmentReview, Sec.Core.ProfileIncomplete) and sends through IC-TRK-04 SendEvent; SEC sends nothing directly and respects TRK-006 preferences, with breach notices to people as a mandatory category where the country profile requires notice (BR-TRK-031).
basis: Proposed; owner decision Messages outside TRK

rule: Feature state: SEC features that are not always on (SEC-005, SEC-009, SEC-010, SEC-014, SEC-015) check IC-PLT-02 IsEnabled for the store before showing pages or running scheduled work. Audit capture (SEC-004), transport and card-data rules, consent tools, the country profile, breach handling, captcha and the upload controls are always on and cannot be switched off.

The Marketplace pack (SEL features except SEL-013) is installed for a client, and VendorSettings.AllowCustomersToApplyForVendorAccount switched on, only after the client confirms a marketplace seller model (KG-01 KTDA, MG-02 Malawi Post).

A vendor becomes active only through SEL approval: Vendor.Active is set to true only by the SEL-003 Approved transition (all required documents Accepted, current seller terms accepted, list check passed). A SEL action filter on Admin VendorController.Create and Edit [POST] refuses Active = true otherwise (message Sel.ActivationBlocked). Vendors created in admin get an application record Under Review. A vendor with Active = false and no application record is treated as Submitted. The same filter refuses Active = false on Edit and refuses Delete [POST] for a vendor whose application is Approved (message Sel.UseSuspension): an approved seller leaves the marketplace only by suspension or blacklisting, which pause its listings. Current terms acceptance is read through IC-IAM-05 HasAcceptedCurrent.
basis: REQ-MPC-FR-028; REQ-MPC-FR-030; FIT (Admin VendorController.Edit/Create take VendorModel; Delete soft-deletes without unpublishing products); ONE-RECORD; Proposed

rule: Segregation of duties in verification: an appeal is not decided by the reviewer who made the decision appealed; a reviewer cannot decide an application of a seller to which the reviewer's customer account is linked.

Required profile fields are native required vendor attributes (supported controls: drop-down, radio, checkboxes, text box, multiline; file upload and date picker are excluded natively); required documents are SEL document types per seller type and tier.
basis: REQ-MPC-FR-036; FIT (VendorAttribute admin view excludes FileUpload, Datepicker, ColorSquares, ImageSquares)

rule: SEL never sets Product.Published. It is a provider to the CAT-002 IProductService override (decision OVR-REG) and requests pause and resume of a seller's listings from the CAT-022 lifecycle service (IC-CAT-03 PauseListings / ResumeListings for the vendor, BR-CAT-030) with a reason code (Vacation, SellerSuspended, SellerBlacklisted, DocumentExpired, CommissionOverdue, PerformanceIntervention). A listing resumes only when no pause reason remains. While any reason remains, every publish path (admin create and edit, bulk edit, import, and native low-stock republish in ProductService.ApplyLowStockActivityAsync) must keep the product unpublished.
basis: FIT (ProductService.UpdateProductAsync is the common path; low-stock activity sets Published); Proposed

rule: Suspension sets Vendor.Active = false and pauses listings with reason SellerSuspended. Both are needed: Vendor.Active = false challenges seller users in admin (ValidateVendor) and hides the vendor page, but ProductService.SearchProductsAsync does not filter products by vendor status. In 5.00 the AI-provider and search-provider results are joined to the same published, ACL and store query, so a paused (unpublished) listing stays hidden on every search path.

Maker-checker: a payout account change and an override of a NotVerified identity check (or of a manual review outcome NotConfirmed; an Inconclusive result goes to manual review first, decision ONE-RECORD) take effect only after approval by an authorised user who is not the requester and not linked to the seller. Payout account changes are approved in ADM-006 (IC-ADM-03); SEL re-checks the rule in the OnApproved callback. Payouts use only Verified accounts.
Payout account identifiers and KYC identifiers are stored encrypted and shown masked except to users with the approving permission; they are never exported in configuration packs.

Marketplace rules are versioned; each publish creates a new version shown on the rule summary page; listing eligibility is checked against the current version at publish. A product passes only if every active rule passes, and the native checks (Category.RestrictFromVendors, VendorSettings.MaximumProductNumber) also apply.

Seller staff users have Customer.VendorId of the seller and are in the native Vendors role, so the native ValidateVendor filter challenges them when the vendor is inactive. Per-user limits come from a staff profile and are enforced by a SEL global action filter on admin and seller-portal actions. Native fact: all customers linked to a vendor otherwise share the same vendor rights. A staff user is never given a non-Vendors role with admin access, because GetCurrentVendorAsync returns null for an inactive vendor and the user would then see unscoped data.

Commission and fee rule resolution: the most specific matching rule applies (seller, seller type or tier, listing or service type, category, default); rules are versioned with an effective date and an order line keeps the versions in force at order placement.

Settlement amount = sum of seller shares of eligible PAY-010 splits, minus refund reversals, minus fee charges (SEL-016), minus seller charges supplied through IC-SEL-05 (ORD-004 SellerPenalty, FIN-001 repayment deduction capped at the lowest of the instructed amount (for basis Share: the instructed share of the batch net, computed by SEL-017 when the batch is calculated; Proposed), the outstanding balance and the batch net, RET merchant-paid return charge or seller-fault remedy), plus or minus adjustments. Service lines are eligible only when Accepted (BR-SVC-041). Splits whose payment was allocated to a receivable Assigned to a lender (BR-PAY-131) are excluded. Each split and each charge is included in exactly one batch. A zero or negative net is carried forward.
basis: D; Proposed; ORD, FIN, RET and SVC

rule: A payout is sent only for a released batch, to the Verified default payout account snapshot taken at release, through IC-PAY-01 Payout with idempotency key batch ID + attempt number.
KPI thresholds have a KPI, comparator, value, period and action (Warn, PauseListings, Suspend). Suspend only proposes; compliance staff confirm.
A seller rating can be given only by the buyer of the order, once per order and seller, after OrderStatus Complete; moderation follows the approval setting.

List types: Block prevents the actions in its scope; Watch raises a review flag without blocking; Allow suppresses Watch flags for the subject (Proposed). Entries have start and optional end, expire automatically, and every change is audited. Block messages do not state the reason.

Blacklisting a seller suspends it, pauses its listings and adds its identifiers (owner and staff email and phone, registration number, payout account identifiers) as linked Block entries with the same period.
Vacation pauses listings with reason Vacation and does not change Vendor.Active; the notice is shown on the vendor page and, where unpublished product pages are viewable, on product pages.
Only Approved, unexpired panel members of a category are invited to quote for requests in that category.
Import rows are validated field by field; a row whose email or phone matches an existing customer or another row is a duplicate and creates no invitation.

For orders paid by direct payment, commission and fees accrue per line at the rule versions in force at order placement and are invoiced per seller per period; invoices are receivables in PAY-033 and fiscal documents through PAY-025 where E-INV applies.

Seller notifications use the native vendor templates for order events (sent through the TRK-005 IWorkflowMessageService override) and TRK-005 for every other event and channel: SEL registers its event codes at installation through IC-TRK-04 RegisterEventCode (names Proposed, listed in BR-TRK-023: Sel.ApplicationApproved.SellerNotification, Sel.ApplicationRejected.SellerNotification, Sel.DocumentExpiring.SellerNotification, Sel.PayoutAccountChangePending.SellerNotification, Sel.PanelExpiring.SellerNotification, Sel.Core.VerificationDecided, Sel.Core.DocumentResubmissionRequested, Sel.Core.DocumentRejected, Sel.Core.DocumentExpired, Sel.Core.PayoutAccountChangeDecided, Sel.Core.SettlementPaid, Sel.Core.SettlementFailed, Sel.Core.CommissionInvoiceIssued, Sel.Core.CommissionInvoiceOverdue, Sel.Core.KpiWarning, Sel.Core.AppealDecided, Sel.Core.ComplaintRegistered, Sel.Core.Invitation) and sends through IC-TRK-04 SendEvent. SEL sends no message itself; TRK-006 preferences and opt-outs apply (MSG-ROUTE).
Diversity characteristics are vendor attributes declared by the seller; reports show shares, never individual values, to users without Marketplace.Core.Applications.View.
A fulfilment service is offered for opt-in only where the client marks it available for the seller's location area.

SEL plugins (Marketplace pack and the Platform core part holding SEL-013): (a) check feature state through IC-PLT-02 IsEnabled (setting productfeature.<prd-id>, store then shared) before showing a page or widget or running a scheduled task for a store; (b) list every new setting key in the plugin key catalogue with key, type, layer, secret flag and default; no SEL setting holds a credential, and payout and KYC identifiers are data, never settings (BR-SEL-008); (c) list every SEL action filter and provider registration in the ADM extension register (BR-ADM-001); SEL registers no DI override of a native service (decision OVR-REG).

Keyword search runs through IProductService.SearchProductsAsync. Without a provider it is the native database search: LIKE (string.Contains) on names (and descriptions or tags only when the advanced options are ticked), equality on SKU and manufacturer part number, localized names when two or more languages are published. With the SRC provider selected (CatalogSettings.ActiveSearchProviderSystemName), keyword search on the storefront, in suggestions and in the search API uses the provider; admin searches (showHidden) always use the native search. In 5.00 an active AI recommendation provider is called before the ISearchProvider (BR-SRC-150).

The provider returns product IDs in relevance order for the keywords only. Native code then applies store mapping, ACL, published, deleted, availability dates, category, manufacturer, price and specification filters; the provider order is kept only when the sort is "position". A provider error or an empty provider result falls back to the native search when CatalogSettings.UseStandardSearchWhenNoResults is on (5.00 name of UseStandardSearchWhenSearchProviderThrowsException).
Filters combine with OR inside one attribute and AND across attributes and filter types (native for specification attributes; Proposed for seller, in-stock and location).

"In stock" = the product does not manage stock, or allows backorders, or GetTotalStockQuantityAsync (including INV unsellable-lot rules) is above 0; for products managed by attributes, at least one combination has stock above 0 or allows out-of-stock orders.

Seller, in-stock, location, eligibility and new sort options are implemented as search filter and ordering providers (IC-SRC-02) registered as IC-CAT-04 search filter / ordering contributors with the single IProductService override owned by CAT-002 (decision OVR-REG, BR-CAT-031); the host applies them before ordering and paging and not when showHidden is true; SRC does not override IProductService itself. The filter state comes from the request (query string) through a scoped search context. Every SRC provider, override and action filter is listed in the ADM extension register (BR-ADM-001).

Product location = the warehouses holding sellable stock of the product (INV-002 coordinates and address); district = the address field configured per client; nearby pickup = pickup points linked to such warehouses. Distance is great-circle distance in kilometres.
Popularity = units sold in the configured period (order lines of non-cancelled orders); origin = the value of the specification attribute configured as origin. Native sort values are unchanged.

Boosting rules have a dimension (category, featured, location), a weight, an on/off state and a version; synonyms are groups per language. Every create, change, enable or disable is a new version and is audited (AUD-SRC-001). Boosting changes order only, never which products are eligible.

A product is eligible for results, recommendations and lists only if published (Product.Published is true only while the CAT listing state is Published, BR-CAT-005), not deleted, inside its availability dates and allowed by store mapping and ACL; out-of-stock products are excluded from search results only when the client rule is on. Products of a suspended seller are excluded because SEL-003 pauses their listings (BR-SEL-006); SRC applies no vendor-status filter of its own.

With SRC-016 active, the category tree changes only through approved proposals; native Admin CategoryController Create, Edit, Delete, DeleteSelected and ImportFromXlsx [POST] are refused by an SRC global action filter (Src.UseTaxonomyWorkflow). Approver and proposer must differ. The filter is listed in the ADM extension register (BR-ADM-001).

Dated placements (banners, featured categories, featured sellers, campaign pages, badges with end date) are shown only when the current time in the store time zone is between start and end; an open end means no end.
Personalisation events are sent only while the customer's personalisation consent is given; withdrawal stops sending at once and triggers a deletion request to the service.

The search API returns only what the storefront search would return for the same store and language; every call carries a valid INT-001 token with scope search.read; calls above the INT-001 per-client rate limit are refused (BR-INT-002, BR-INT-004).
Search requests on the storefront have a client-side timeout and a retry limit (settings); the typed text is never lost on failure.

Every SRC page, widget, action filter, search provider, IC-SRC-02 provider and scheduled task checks the state of its feature for the store through IC-PLT-02 (setting productfeature.<prd-id>, store then shared value) before it acts; when the feature is off the provider returns the query unchanged. Every new SRC setting key is listed in the SRC key catalogue (key, type, layer, secret flag, default); credentials and keys (recommendation service, API signing) are flagged secret (BR-PLT-013, CFG-01).

Erasure and consent withdrawal: SRC registers a provider of IAM IC-IAM-08 (ErasePersonalData, ConsentWithdrawn). On erasure it deletes the customer's recent search terms (SRC-012), saved searches and alerts (SRC-011) and personalisation records, and, when a recommendation provider is registered, passes a deletion request for the pseudonymous data to it (IC-SRC-04 DeleteSubjectData; AI-007 forwards it through IC-AI-03); on withdrawal of the personalisation consent it stops events at once (BR-SRC-080). From 5.00 the native SearchTerm rows carry the customer id and are the SRC-012 history; native erasure does not delete them, so the SRC provider hard-deletes the customer's SearchTerm rows through IRepository<SearchTerm>.DeleteAsync(predicate). A provider failure keeps the IAM request InProgress.

Search path configuration rule (VER-500): SearchProductsAsync calls the AI recommendation provider (ArtificialIntelligenceSettings.ActiveAIRecommendationProviderSystemName) before the ISearchProvider for every storefront keyword search, suggestion and search-API call. Every configuration pack sets ArtificialIntelligenceSettings.UseStandardSearchWhenNoResults and CatalogSettings.UseStandardSearchWhenNoResults on, because with the AI setting off a failed or empty AI search returns products without any keyword filter. The Google AI Commerce Search plugin is selected only for a client that has confirmed the transfer of catalogue data and visitor IDs to Google (Not stated in source); then the client names it or the SRC provider as the primary relevance engine of the store, and SRC boosting rules and synonyms apply only on the SRC provider path.

All SRC plugin tables are written through IRepository<>, so the SEC decorator captures old and new values (BR-SEC-010); SRC writes no data through INopDataProvider directly (provider index files are not audited data). Business events AUD-SRC-nnn are written through IC-SEC-01 IAuditTrail.WriteAsync with the request correlation id (BR-SEC-014).

Pricing model per service: Fixed, Per time unit (hour, day, week), Per unit (configurable unit label), From-price (native, attribute-driven), Price on request. Line total = unit price × quantity; for Per time unit the quantity is the number of units covered by the booked slot.

A Price on request service keeps CallForPrice and DisableBuyButton off (both fail the cart warnings that PlaceOrderAsync re-runs); SVC hides the price and refuses direct add-to-cart; only lines created from an accepted quote enter the cart.

A resource counts as available for a slot only if it is active, linked to the service, holds every valid qualification the service requires, works in that slot, covers the location, and has capacity left after holds and bookings.

Bookings are held, confirmed, moved, given an outcome and released only through the CAT-027 booking service IC-CAT-07 (Hold, Confirm, Move, RecordOutcome, Release, WriteSlots) under ILocker key 'cat-slot-{SlotId}' (BR-CAT-021); SVC never writes Booking or BookingSlot capacity directly; IC-SVC-01 GenerateSlots writes slots through IC-CAT-07 WriteSlots. The SVC column on the CAT Booking is Outcome (SM-SVC-02); the Booking Status (SM-CAT-05) is CAT's.
Cancellation, reschedule, no-show, deposit, sign-off, reminder and service-level policies are versioned with an effective date; a booking or order keeps the versions in force when it was made.

Refund on cancellation = amount paid for the booking minus the cancellation fee, never below zero; SVC raises BookingCancellation, ProviderNoShow and DepositRefund refunds through IC-RET-04 RaiseRefundTrigger with the order lines and the amount SVC computes; ServiceFailure triggers are created by RET-005 from the SVC module event Service.Failed; SVC never calls PAY-016 directly and never changes the order payment status.
basis: D; RET-005 (single refund-trigger owner); FIT (PAY BR-PAY-010)

rule: Provider cancellation or provider no-show gives a full refund of the amount paid for the booking and a fee-free rebook offer.
Deposit and balance are separate orders linked by the booking; each order is paid in full natively; the booking is fully paid when the sum of paid plan orders equals the plan total.
basis: Proposed; FIT (PaymentStatus has no partly-paid state)

rule: At the confirm step the unit price of every booking line must equal the amount due under its plan; otherwise the order is not placed.

Service progress is the SVC-005 line stage (stage set and transitions from ORD-002 through IC-ORD-10, BR-ORD-014), not the native OrderStatus, which becomes Complete at payment for orders without shippable items.
A service line is eligible for the provider settlement (SEL-017) only when Accepted; NotDelivered or Failed lines are not paid out.

Downloads follow native rules: activation when paid or manually, maximum count, expiry from the paid date (when paid) or the order date (manual), user agreement, owner check when DownloadableProductsValidateUser is on.

Rental availability for each day of a requested period = hire units minus units on overlapping non-cancelled order lines and active holds of other customers; a request with any day at zero is refused.

Voucher codes are unique per store, not guessable and include a check character; a voucher can be redeemed only by the vendor of its service (or outlet staff for operator services), within validity, while uses remain.
At most one reminder per lead time and one feedback request per line; customer channel preferences (TRK-006) always apply.

Every SVC page, widget, seller-portal or outlet action, action filter and scheduled task checks the feature state of the PRD feature it serves through IC-PLT-02 IsEnabled (setting productfeature.<prd-id>, store value else client value) before it runs for a store; when off, nothing is shown and tasks skip that store. Native product fields used by SVC (price, download, rental) are not switched by it.

Every new SVC setting key (ServicesSettings) is listed in the SVC plugin key catalogue with key, type, layer, secret flag and default, so pack validation accepts it (PLT-003, NFR-X-008). SVC holds no credential, key or token setting. Per-service values are rows of SVC entities (ServicePolicy, ServicePricing, RentalCapacity), not setting keys. Keys are listed in §10.

Each service order line has a response clock and a completion clock; a clock is Met when its stage is reached before the due time, otherwise Breached; escalation levels are notified in order.

Common event codes (Proposed; source terms in brackets): CREATED, ACCEPTED (drop-off, hand-over), PICKED_UP, ARRIVED_HUB, DEPARTED_HUB (hand-over at hubs), IN_TRANSIT, CUSTOMS_HELD, CUSTOMS_CLEARED, OUT_FOR_DELIVERY, ATTEMPT_FAILED (with reason code), READY_FOR_PICKUP, DELIVERED, COLLECTED, RETURNED_TO_SENDER, EXCEPTION, CORRECTION. Each source has a mapping table from its codes to these codes.

An event is a duplicate if its source event id was already received from the same source, or, when no id is given, if an event with the same shipment, code, event time and location exists. Duplicates change nothing.

Applying an event changes native shipment state only forwards and only through IOrderProcessingService (ShipAsync for the first "shipped" code on a non-pickup order; ReadyForPickupAsync for READY_FOR_PICKUP on a pickup order; DeliverAsync for DELIVERED or COLLECTED after BR-LOG-080), under ILocker key 'shipment-{ShipmentId}'. Every product shipping-rate method and pickup provider returns the TRK hub tracker from GetShipmentTrackerAsync so native shipment pages show the hub timeline; TRK does not override IShipmentService (owner ORD-010, OVR-REG) or IOrderProcessingService (owner CHK-003); if the CHK-003 override refuses a call through an ORD hook (for example an ORD-010 hold), the event stays Applied in the timeline and the refusal is listed in the operations queue for retry. Events from the public API (INT-001, scope shipments.write) and PostGlobal (INT-007) follow the same rule; those modules never change shipment state.
Tracking events follow the PLT-020 retention rules: active period, then archive (still searchable by staff), then deletion; each run is logged.

Every notification goes through the engine (the only messages outside it are those of BR-TRK-026): the TRK plugin overrides IWorkflowMessageService (derived from WorkflowMessageService, override of SendNotificationAsync, INopStartup Order ≥ 3000). For each send the engine finds the notification definition for the template name (native templates, and plugin message templates sent through IWorkflowMessageService such as PAY Pay.RefundAfterCancel.CustomerNotification and the CAT Catalogue.* templates) or product event code (IC-TRK-04), applies TRK-006 preferences, renders each channel variant with the same tokens in the customer language, sends, and logs (TRK-007). It returns the queued email id when email is sent, otherwise 0. The override keeps the optional parameter ignoreDelayBeforeSend and passes it on: the 5.00 reminder senders set it to true because the reminder task has already applied the delay. The senders added in 5.00 (SendAbandonedCartFollowUpCustomerNotificationAsync, SendPendingOrderFollowUpCustomerNotificationAsync, SendIncompleteRegistrationNotificationMessageAsync, SendNextRecurringPaymentNotificationCustomerMessageAsync, SendWithdrawalRequestConfirmationNotificationAsync) all end in SendNotificationAsync, so their templates reach the engine like any native template; the forum and news senders left core (forum and news templates are sent by the bundled Misc.Forums and Misc.News plugins, which also call IWorkflowMessageService.SendNotificationAsync).

Order-kind action for native order templates: modules that own an order kind (EGV e-Government applications, SVC service orders) register an order-kind provider (IC-TRK-05). When OrderCompleted.CustomerNotification is triggered for an order whose lines all belong to one registered kind, the engine applies the action configured for that kind: Send (native template), Suppress (logged Suppressed, reason order kind), or Substitute (the substitute definition of the kind is sent instead). No default is set (Not stated in source).

No-email route: when a native template reaches the engine with an empty recipient email address, the email channel is skipped (no QueuedEmail is created) and the SMS variant is sent to Customer phone, else billing address phone; with no SMS variant or no phone the message is logged Failed with reason no address. TRK installs SMS variants for OrderPlaced, OrderPaid, ShipmentSent, CustomerPasswordRecovery and the GDPR customer templates (Proposed content).

Pages without sign-in (tracking number, share link, guest lookup) show no customer name, address, phone or email (a masked contact at most); repeated lookups from one client address beyond a setting require a CAPTCHA.

Preference order (applied by the engine and by IC-TRK-06 CheckAllowed): a mandatory category is always sent on its primary channel; otherwise a message is sent on a channel only if the customer (or, if unset, the client default) allows that category on that channel, the channel is opted in where it needs opt-in (WhatsApp, Telegram, push, voice), SMS is not opted out (customer preference, or a ContactOptOut record for the phone number, BR-TRK-033), and the customer has not unsubscribed from that order's updates. Channel order: the customer's event-level preference, else the IAM-015 default preferred channel, else the definition order.

Messages outside the engine (decision MSG-ROUTE, Proposed): TRK-005 sends every notification. Only two kinds of message may be sent without it: (1) conversational replies in a conversation the customer started: CHN channel replies through IC-CHN-04 SendReply (CRM agents, AI-003 chatbot), CHN-005 replies to inbound SMS commands, and CRM agent e-mail replies on a ticket through the native e-mail account (BR-CRM-004); (2) IAM one-time codes sent to CHN-005 through IC-IAM-01 (BR-IAM-150); where IAM uses the native 5.00 phone one-time-code flow, the code is sent by CustomerController through the core ISmsService to the primary ISmsProvider, which is the CHN-005 aggregator plugin, and that plugin makes the CheckAllowed call (see CHN-005; Presentation/Nop.Web/Controllers/CustomerController.cs:632). Before each such send the sender calls IC-TRK-06 CheckAllowed with the recipient, channel and category (Conversation replies or Security codes, Proposed names) and does not send when Blocked. Quiet hours and message limits (BR-TRK-032) do not apply to them; delivery results stay in the sender's own log (CHN ChannelMessage, IAM OtpChallenge).

Opt-outs of phone numbers without an account (decision MSG-ROUTE): TRK-006 keeps one ContactOptOut record per phone number (international format, BR-IAM-010) and channel, with status (SM-TRK-09), source and time. It is written only through IC-TRK-06 UpdatePreference (CHN-012 keywords, staff on request). A non-mandatory message on that channel to that number is not sent, whether or not the number later belongs to an account; when a customer with that phone number turns the channel on in My account or texts the opt-in keyword, the record becomes OptedIn. No customer record is created for such a number.

Every TRK setting key is listed in the TRK plugin key catalogue (key, type, layer, secret flag, default); source, device and provider credentials are flagged secret, so packs refuse them and exports omit them (BR-PLT-013). TRK pages, widgets and scheduled tasks check the feature state through IC-PLT-02 (productfeature.<prd-id>, per store) before they show or run.

Suppression: a non-urgent message inside the customer's (or default) quiet hours is Held until they end; a non-mandatory message over the customer's limit for the channel and period is Suppressed; urgent messages ignore quiet hours. Held messages are re-checked against preferences when released.
